Instructional planning, organizing and designing instruction, student outcomes instructional principles, and assessing outcomes of effective instruction. Curriculum-based assessment is covered along with the communication of student outcomes. Meets with SPED 4480.

CURR 4065.name: TeachSpecialEd.com: Instructional Strategies: Improving Basic Reading Skills
CURR 4065.description: Emphasizes teaching beginning reading and developing reading fluency. Applicable to teaching students with exceptional learning needs in varied instructional settings. Meets with SPED 4560.

CURR 4066.name: TeachSpecialEd.com: Instructional Strategies: Improving Reading Comprehension
CURR 4066.description: Provides an overview of reading comprehension with emphasis on teaching students with exceptional learning needs. Attention is given to building a knowledge base and analyzing text to enable comprehension skills and teaching comprehension strategies. Meets with SPED 4570.

CURR 4067.name: TeachSpecialEd.com: Language and Communication in Diverse Learners
CURR 4067.description: Places the needs of exceptional learners in the larger context of cultural differences and diversity with a focus on language and communication. Language development and communication styles are covered. Teaching second language learners. Augmentative, alternative and assistive communication development is addressed. Meets with SPED 4580.

CURR 4068.name: TeachSpecialEd.com: Collaboration and Instructional Planning in Individual Education Programs (IEP)
CURR 4068.description: Emphasizes developing standards-based IEPs in accordance with Idea requirements. Introduces models of collaboration and highlights developing collaboration skills to enhance effectiveness of the beginning teacher in development and implementation of IEPs. Meets with SPED 4860.

CURR 4069.name: TeachSpecialEd.com: Professional and Ethical Practices
CURR 4069.description: Focuses on the ethical standards and principles of the profession. Ethical issues related to assessment, decision making, instruction, working with agencies, and families/guardians of children with exceptional learning needs are covered. Meets with SPED 4870.

CURR 4100.name: Introduction to Technology in Education
CURR 4100.description: Covers the fundamental concepts of computer uses in education. The course is designed for practicing or prospective educators who wish to explore computer uses in the classroom. Demonstrations of classroom activities, modern applications, and electronic mail will be conducted.

CURR 4102.name: Selected Topics in Education Technology
CURR 4102.description: Offered by guest lecturers to the university or by regular faculty where special topics or special needs arise. Examples of appropriate topics include the study of hypermedia, desktop publishing in educational settings, the application of microcomputers to a field or subject area, or the study of advanced technologies such as a videodisk integration. Topics and prerequisites to be announced.

CURR 4103.name: Technology for the Learner with Special Needs
CURR 4103.description: Participants will review and synthesize literature on a broad variety of technological solutions that meet the needs of special learners (with different school-based disabilities). Students will also conduct investigations into the use of adaptive devices and assistive technologies, demonstrate their use, and design learning environments to support the learner’s needs for education in the least restrictive environment. Meets with CURR 5122.

CURR 4131.name: Web-Based Delivery of Training
CURR 4131.description: This series of six half-credit modules addresses a range of topics relating to web-based delivery of training. The topic mix for the modules evolves as the technology evolves. Students must take modules in multiples of two. Meets with CURR 5131.

CURR 4440.name: Selected Topics in Reading Education
CURR 4440.description: Selected topics and issues in reading education will be explored in depth. Examples of special topics include: Introduction to Whole Language; Whole Language and Phonics Instruction; Reading; Writing and Spelling Connections; and others as issues arise.
CURR 4440.prereqs: Bachelor’s degree in Education or related field

CURR 4504.name: Topics in Teaching Science
CURR 4504.description: Explores selected topics in science teaching. Topics will vary each time course is offered. Meets with CURR 5504.

CURR 4801.name: Creating Culturally Responsive Pedagogy
CURR 4801.description: Provides educators with a framework for teaching about privilege and oppression. Designed to enhance the commitment to culturally responsive pedagogy and inclusive classrooms. Emphasizes pedagogical approaches to teaching diverse populations. Includes hands-on activities. Meets with CURR 5801.

CYSM 2000.name: Cybersecurity Fundamentals for Business
CYSM 2000.description: Explore and critically assess cybersecurity principles, practices, and strategies necessary for leaders to effectively contribute to cybersecurity programs. Topics include cybersecurity fundamentals, IT governance, data security, and security education. Students will examine and synthesize knowledge to develop strategic management skills using current cybersecurity frameworks.

CYSM 2950.name: Topics in Cybersecurity Management
CYSM 2950.description: Experimental courses offered irregularly at the Sophomore level for the purpose of presenting new subject matter in cybersecurity management. Course prerequisites will vary depending upon topics covered.

CYSM 3500.name: Introduction to Cybersecurity Technologies
CYSM 3500.description: This course provides instruction in security for network hardware, software, and data including physical security, software protections, and process implementation. Identification of exposures and vulnerabilities and appropriate countermeasures are addressed. The focus is on incorporating security technology into an organization’s IT infrastructure.

CYSM 3600.name: Cloud Computing & Security
CYSM 3600.description: This course introduces students to underlying technologies and concepts of cloud computing. It explores fundamental principles, architecture and technological mechanisms of cloud computing. Students will learn about cloud security threats and how to defend against cloud-specific cyber-attacks. The course will evaluate various cloud delivery models and discuss business value of cloud computing. Students will gain hands-on experience with in-demand cloud applications and tools.

CYSM 3750.name: Organizational Cybersecurity
CYSM 3750.description: Organizations and their employees are faced with risks associated with the modern, digital working environment. This course introduces fundamental cyber security concepts, the risks they present, and policies and practices employed to mitigate the risks for both individuals and their organizations.

CYSM 3950.name: Topics in Cybersecurity Management- Undergraduate
CYSM 3950.description: Experimental courses offered irregularly at the undergraduate level for the purpose of presenting new subject matter in cybersecurity management.
CYSM 3950.prereqs: Business Students only and Junior standing

CYSM 4100.name: IT Risk Management
CYSM 4100.description: This course is focused on effectively managing information risks in an organization. It provides an overview of risk issues and emphasizes understanding of information risk as a socio-technical issue. The course covers risk assessment, risk perception and communication, economic aspects of risk, and risk management. It presents different methodologies and approaches to risk management. Students will learn about risk mitigation techniques along with potential organizational barriers.

CYSM 4300.name: IT Security Auditing
CYSM 4300.description: This course will focus on the fundamental concepts related to auditing information systems and IT infrastructures in both the public and private sector. We will also discuss principles and practices related to secure operation of existing information technology. The course will cover identification of appropriate IS security audit standards, controls, and procedures for a secure information system. This course will prepare students to skillfully complete a cyber security audit. INFS 3070 is a recommended prerequisite.

CYSM 4500.name: Ethical Hacking
CYSM 4500.description: This course is an introduction to the fundamentals of ethical hacking. It focuses on the knowledge and skills required to understand the mechanics behind hacking attacks. Students will learn about tools and vulnerabilities of software and networks used by hackers to access unauthorized information. The course is designed to be hands-on to enhance familiarity with penetration testing and other hacking tools. It also addresses incident handling methods and system defense to prevent computer attacks.

CYSM 4700.name: Cloud Computing & Security
CYSM 4700.description: This course introduces students to underlying technologies and concepts of cloud computing. It explores fundamental principles, architecture and technological mechanisms of cloud computing. Students will learn about cloud security threats and how to defend against cloud-specific cyber-attacks. The course will evaluate various cloud delivery models and discuss business value of cloud computing. Students will gain hands-on experience with in-demand cloud applications and tools.

CYSM 4950.name: Topics in Cybersecurity Management- Undergraduate
CYSM 4950.description: Experimental courses offered irregularly at the undergraduate level for the purpose of presenting new subject matter in cybersecurity management. Second semester junior or senior standing required. Course prerequisites will vary depending upon topics covered.
CYSM 4950.prereqs: Business Students Only and Junior Standing

DNCE 1000.name: Dance Appreciation: From Ballet to Beyoncé
DNCE 1000.description: This introductory course focuses on the role of dance as part of human identity. How does dance affect you? How do different cultures use dance to communicate, express, protest, and celebrate? How does dance intersect with visual arts, music, theater? Approved for LAS Humanities area requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore- Arts, Humanities, and Cultures.

DNCE 2700.name: Fundamentals of Dance Technique
DNCE 2700.description: An introduction to dance technique. Students will focus on technique exercises, stretching, body alignment, choreography, and movement explorations. The course is a beginning dance class and the foundation for other dance classes. Additional outside work required. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Arts, Humanities, and Cultures.

DNCE 2720.name: Modern Dance I
DNCE 2720.description: The class is designed to provide a foundation of modern dance technique. Students will experience full dance classes consisting of warm-up, technique exercises, stretching, body alignment, center exercises and cool down. Students will also participate in movement explorations through improvisation.. Additional outside work required. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Explore-Arts, Humanities, and Cultures.

DNCE 2740.name: Ballet I
DNCE 2740.description: Introduces the basic techniques of ballet, which are built upon knowledge of ballet terminology, fundamental exercises, and the basic elements of  dance. Focuses on movement-oriented dance, comprised of stretching, barre warm-up exercises, simple terre a terre and jumping steps, and basic extended positions. Additional outside work required. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Explore-Arts, Humanities, and Cultures.

DNCE 2770.name: Afro-Brazilian Dances
DNCE 2770.description: Studio course that introduces the movement vocabulary, cultural, and social aspects of specific styles of Afro-Brazilian Dances: Jongo, Côco de Roda, Caboclinhos, and Orixá Dances. Readings, video viewing, writing, and in-class creative projects will inform the main focus of the course, movement exploration. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity).

DNCE 2900.name: Special Topics in Dance Technique
DNCE 2900.description: Focus is on various forms of dance. Each semester the course will use technique, research, and performance to highlight a specific dance genre. For both beginners and advanced. No prerequisites for this course.

DNCE 3201.name: Topics in Early Dance History
DNCE 3201.description: The course explores special topics related to the history of dance ranging from ancient times to  the end of the 19th century. The course examines key topics in Western theatrical dance history as well as Transnational forms. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Writing Intensive.

DNCE 3202.name: Topics in Contemporary Dance History:
DNCE 3202.description: The course explores special topics related to modern and postmodern history of dance, mainly from the 20th century. The course examines key topics in Western theatrical dance history as well as Transnational forms.

DNCE 3390.name: Dance Performance Practicum
DNCE 3390.description: Students will receive practical experience as a dancer in a project approved by the program. Enrollment by audition and/or permission of instructor.

DNCE 3391.name: Dance Technical Practicum
DNCE 3391.description: Students will receive practical experience as a technician in a project approved by the program. Enrollment by audition and/or permission of instructor.

DNCE 3392.name: Dance Choreography Practicum
DNCE 3392.description: Students will receive practical experience as a choreographer or assistant choreographer in a project approved by the program. Enrollment by audition and/or permission of instructor.

DNCE 3700.name: Special Topics in Dance Technique
DNCE 3700.description: Focus is on various forms of dance. Each semester the course will use technique, research, and performance to highlight a specific dance genre.

DNCE 3720.name: Advanced Modern Dance
DNCE 3720.description: The class is designed for dancers who are at an intermediate to advanced level in modern dance technique and is a continuation of DNCE 3710. Students will participate in movement explorations where they can creatively engage the fundamentals of space, time and force through improvisation. The course will culminate in a modern dance performance. Additional outside work required.
DNCE 3720.prereqs: DNCE 2700, DNCE 3710, or consent of instructor

DNCE 3730.name: Jazz Dance Technique
DNCE 3730.description: Introduces the basic techniques of jazz dance, which are built upon knowledge of jazz terminology, rhythm, fundamental exercises, and the basic elements of dance. The course will culminate in a jazz dance performance. Additional outside work required.

DNCE 3750.name: Tap Dance
DNCE 3750.description: An introduction to the basic techniques of tap dance that progresses through intermediate and advanced terminology. In addition to performance, the class considers tap history and its position as an American art form.

DNCE 3760.name: Hip Hop
DNCE 3760.description: This course explores specific technique, vocabulary, creative processes, musicality and dynamics of hip hop. Styles include dancing, locking, popping, hip hop and house techniques, as well as historical contexts.

DNCE 3770.name: Samba
DNCE 3770.description: Samba is an umbrella term that encompasses different Afro-Brazilian dances. This studio course introduces the movement vocabulary, cultural, and social aspects of specific styles of Samba. Readings, video viewing, writing, and in-class creative projects will inform movement exploration.

DNCE 3800.name: Contemporary Styles: Jazz, Lyrical, and Modern Dance
DNCE 3800.description: With a particular emphasis on jazz, lyrical, and modern styles, this course considers a range of contemporary dance techniques and assesses their overlaps and influences on one another. The course culminates in a presentation.

DNCE 4393.name: Dance Capstone
DNCE 4393.description: Students will receive practical experience in a culminating project that will be adjudicated by the Theatre and Dance faculty. Enrollment by audition and/or permission of instructor.

DNCE 4700.name: Dance Composition I
DNCE 4700.description: Students will study and apply the basic choreographic elements that go into creating an original dance. In a laboratory type setting, students will work on developing their own artistic voices through short movement compositions as well as give critique to others. Additional outside work required.

DNCE 4710.name: Dance Composition 2
DNCE 4710.description: Students study and apply advanced choreographic elements that go into creating an original dance. Building on level one composition, this culminating course ends with a dance showcase.

DNCE 4720.name: Modern Dance II
DNCE 4720.description: Building on modern dance foundations, this class introduces dancers to advance principles and exercises. Students will participate in movement explorations where they can creatively engage the fundamentals of space, time and force through improvisation. Culminates in a modern dance performance. Additional outside work required.

DNCE 4740.name: Ballet II
DNCE 4740.description: Building on ballet foundations, this class introduces dancers to advanced ballet principles and exercises intended to develop harmony, stylistic specificity and artistry. Excerpts from the classical repertoire will be used to promote musicality and artistic expression.

DNCE 4900.name: Spec Tpcs in Music and Dance:
DNCE 4900.description: Through the study of historical and contemporary convergences across music, sound, dance and movement, students will develop collaborative languages and methods in order to build and articulate original works. Topics will vary each semester.

DASE 1011.name: Introduction Data Analytics and Systems Engineering
DASE 1011.description: Introduction to data analytics and systems engineering. Basic methods used for descriptive, predictive and diagnostic data analysis. Engineering complex systems. Exploring the importance of collecting, understanding and analyzing data in engineering complex systems using simple robotic systems.

DASE 2020.name: Introduction to Statistics for Data Analytics
DASE 2020.description: Introduction to statistics for data analytics using R Studio and SPSS. Includes basic statistics, distributions, statistical tests, variance and hypothesis testing (t-, chi^2, F tests), and ANOVA, an introduction to descriptive and predictive analytics and linear probability mixed models.
DASE 2020.prereqs: CS 1120 or ECE 1021 or instructor permission (equivalent programming experience required)

DASE 2021.name: Computer Based Modeling in C
DASE 2021.description: Emphasis on algorithm development and H/W implementation of C programs for solving engineering problems. Students learn to write structured C programs using: arrays, user functions, pointers, data structures, file 1/0 and multi-file compiles. Meets with ECE 2021.

DASE 3003.name: Advanced Robotics
DASE 3003.description: Explore advanced robotics topics through the project management process. Project based class with scheduled milestones, min. lecture, max. applied. For the final project, each student will build and program a small autonomous vehicle to navigate between GPS coordinates.
DASE 3003.prereqs: ECE 2021 or DASE 2021 or Permission of Instructor

DASE 3005.name: C++ & GUI Programming
DASE 3005.description: A hands-on course in C++ programming and GUI development integrating hardware and software. Students implement programs on a Raspberry Pi with a Touchscreen. Basic computer architecture and the Linux OS are covered. Min. lecture, max. applied.
DASE 3005.prereqs: DASE 2021 or ECE 2021 or ECE 1021 or Permission of Instructor

DASE 3007.name: Python & Jupyter Programming
DASE 3007.description: A hands-on course in Python programming and Jupyter Notebook development using various add-on libraries; integrating hardware and software. Students implement programs on a Raspberry Pi with a touch screen. Basic computer architecture and the Linux OS are covered. Min. lecture, max. applied.
DASE 3007.prereqs: DASE 2021 or ECE 2021 or ECE 1021 or Permission of Instructor

DASE 3009.name: IoT on AWS
DASE 3009.description: A hands-on course in Amazon Web Services (AWS) Internet of Things (loT) programming; integrating hardware and software. Students initiate programs on a Raspberry Pi, through AWS, to different types of loT devices. Min. lecture, max. applied.
DASE 3009.prereqs: ECE 1021 or ECE 2021 or DASE 2021 or Permission of Instructor

DASE 4000.name: Introduction to Operations Research
DASE 4000.description: An introduction to quantitative modeling methods (i.e., mathematical programming, optimization, queuing, simulation, decision analysis) with broad application. The course focuses on the computer implementation of models, and the application of models to practical decision-making scenarios.
DASE 4000.prereqs: CS 2300 or MATH 3130; ECE 3610 or MATH 3810; DASE students only

DASE 4030.name: Introduction to Systems Engineering
DASE 4030.description: Introduction to the systems engineering process to include systems in engineering methods, lifecycle models, risk management, and tradeoff analysis. Focus is on the role of the systems engineer throughout a project, with emphasis on both the technical and project management roles.

DASE 4435.name: Data Mining
DASE 4435.description: This course covers introduction to fundamental concepts, data warehousing, data pre-processing, association rules, cluster analysis, classification and prediction.

DASE 4460.name: Intelligent Robotics
DASE 4460.description: This course introduces students to the field of robotics.  Topics include Robotics Operating System, Agents and agent-based system, swarm intelligence, Unmanned Vehicles (UGV, UAV, AUV), robot teaming, mission planning/management systems, path planning & obstacle avoidance.
DASE 4460.prereqs: CS 2060, CS 2150 or MATH 2150, MATH 1360, CS 1450, and CS 2300 or MATH 3130

DASE 4470.name: Data Visualization
DASE 4470.description: Animation: basic principles, physically based modeling, algorithms for animation, constraint optimization, use of dynamics in animations, and teleological modeling. Scientific Visualization: overview, foundational techniques, and applications.
DASE 4470.prereqs: CS 2300 or MATH 3130, CS 4720, or instructor consent

DASE 4570.name: Computer-based Optimization
DASE 4570.description: Computer-Based optimization techniques including simulation, modeling, heuristic methods, genetic algorithms, simulated annealing, duality theory, dynamic programming, and queuing theory.

DASE 4710.name: Evolutionary Computation
DASE 4710.description: Introduction to evolutionary computation with emphasis on genetic algorithms. Includes evolution strategies, evolutionary programming, schemata fitness functions and classifiers, current research topics, messy algorithms, adaptive landscapes.
DASE 4710.prereqs: ECE 3610 or MATH 3810 or QUAN 2010; CS 3160; CS 4720 or CS 4820; or Instructor Permission

DASE 4860.name: Machine Learning
DASE 4860.description: Introduction to machine learning followed by a selection of machine learning topics such as regression, Bayesisan learning, Hidden Markov Models, support vector machine, clustering and reinforcement learning.
DASE 4860.prereqs: CS 4820; MATH 2150; MATH 3130 or CS 2300; CS 3160 or instructor consent

DASE 4910.name: Design of Experiments
DASE 4910.description: An introduction to experimentation and the application of statistical design. Topics include design and analysis of single-factor and multi-factor experiments.

ECON 1000.name: The Economics of Social Issues
ECON 1000.description: The Economics of Social Issues introduces the student to economics in a less rigorous manner than ECON 1010. Economic issues are introduced in examining wealth, poverty, energy, crime, education, health, discrimination, unemployment and inflation. May not be taken for credit by students who have already completed ECON 3010. Approved for LAS Social Science area requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Society, Health and Behavior. GT-SS1.

ECON 1010.name: Introduction to Microeconomics
ECON 1010.description: An analysis of the market system and its role in allocating goods and services; problems of market failure (e.g., monopoly, environmental pollution, and public goods), and alternative government responses to such problems. Approved for LAS Social Science area requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Society, Health and Behavior.

ECON 1050.name: Economics in Practice
ECON 1050.description: Designed as a practical introduction to the process of teaching and learning economics through activity-based economic instruction. Covers a variety of economic topics by use of materials developed by National Council on Economic Education. While particularly relevant to prospective teachers of K-12 economics, the class is open to anyone wishing a hands-on approach to economic content. Approved for LAS Social Science area requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Society, Health and Behavior. GT-SS1.
ECON 1050.prereqs: Not open to students who have completed ECON 3010 or ECON 3020

ECON 1310.name: Survey of Economics
ECON 1310.description: An introduction to basic economic principles and problems of contemporary society.  Surveys the fundamentals of private enterprise and the economic role of government in society.  Not eligible for credit if ECON 3010 already completed.

ECON 1320.name: Economics for Leaders
ECON 1320.description: This course introduces basic economics concepts and tools of economic reasoning and applies them within the context of public issues and economic development. Participants receive direct instruction from economists, participate in group activities, presentations, simulations, and discussions.

ECON 1321.name: Economic Forces in American History
ECON 1321.description: This course introduces and applies economic concepts and tools of economic reasoning to pivotal events in history. Participants hear lectures from economic historians, participate in group activities, simulations, and discussions.

ECON 1330.name: Entrepreneurship in the Global Economy
ECON 1330.description: The course focuses on the introduction and application of basic economic concepts and economic reasoning skills to entrepreneurship. The goal of this program is to prepare students to apply economic concepts and economic reasoning to starting a business.

ECON 1340.name: The Environment and the Economy
ECON 1340.description: This course focuses on the introduction of basic economic concepts and economic reasoning skills and their application to the environment. The goal of this program is to present topics on environmental issues and concerns and let them apply the lens of economics to discover how incentives and institutions influence decision-makers. Participants receive direct instruction, participate in group activities, presentations, simulations and discussions to improve their own understanding of current local, national and global environmental issues. Their culminating project involves using economic concepts to analyze a current environmental issue and then proposing a public policy that could improve the outcomes.

ECON 2020.name: Introduction to Macroeconomics
ECON 2020.description: This course provides an examination of the forces that determine national income, unemployment, and inflation; the efforts of the government and the central bank to manage the state of the macroeconomy; and, the influence of the global economy on domestic macroeconomic functioning. Approved for LAS Social Science area requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Society, Health and Behavior.

ECON 2210.name: Personal Economics
ECON 2210.description: Students will learn to apply the economic way of thinking to manage their scarce resources. Employs economic concepts to understand: financial planning and income management; saving and investing; stocks, bonds, and mutual funds; risk-return tradeoff and diversification; interest rates and credit. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Society, Health and Behavior.

ECON 2810.name: Statistics for Economics
ECON 2810.description: Uses of descriptive and inferential statistics in economics. Introduction to probability, random sampling, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing and simple linear regression.

ECON 3010.name: Intermediate Microeconomic Theory
ECON 3010.description: Production, price, and distribution theory under conditions of perfect and imperfect competition.
ECON 3010.prereqs: ECON 1010 or ECON 1050 with a “C” or better

ECON 3020.name: Intermediate Macroeconomic Theory
ECON 3020.description: Keynesian, classical, and monetarist theories of national income determination. Problems of unemployment, inflation, international exchange, and growth.

ECON 3150.name: History of Economic Thought
ECON 3150.description: Surveys the main schools of economic thought from the pre-cursors to the Classical economists through the modern neo-Classical reconciliation. The challenges posed by the Marxian critique and the Keynesian transformation will be considered.  Approved for LAS Social Science area requirement.

ECON 3160.name: Austrian Economics
ECON 3160.description: This course surveys the conceptual analysis of the Austrian School in economics. Topics include the Austrian School perspective on: market process, profit and loss, entrepreneurship, spontaneous order, money, inflation, recession, knowledge, competition, and economic progress.
ECON 3160.prereqs: ECON 1010 with a “C” or better or consent of instructor

ECON 3210.name: Public Sector Economics
ECON 3210.description: This course aims to explore government intervention in the economy, examining the impact of expenditure programs and taxation on citizens. It thoroughly covers the theoretical foundations guiding government involvement, current public finance issues, empirical evaluation of policies, and considers the justification for such intervention.
ECON 3210.prereqs: ECON 1010 or ECON 1050 with a “C” or better

ECON 3280.name: International Political Economy
ECON 3280.description: Overview of the world political economy, especially in the post-WWII period. The central goal of the course is to provide information and develop analytical tools necessary for students to grasp the political issues inherent in international economic relations. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Sustainability.
ECON 3280.prereqs: ECON 1000, ECON 1010 or ECON 2020 with a “C” or better

ECON 3300.name: Environmental Economics
ECON 3300.description: Application of economic analysis to environmental and natural resources issues and policies. Topics include: benefit-cost analysis, property rights, depletable resources, energy resources, toxic substances, air and water pollution.
ECON 3300.prereqs: ECON 1010 with a “C” or better or permission of instructor

ECON 3310.name: Ecological Economics
ECON 3310.description: Applies new knowledge in natural and physical sciences and behavior to all economic resources: labor, capital, and natural resources. Uses new analytical tools such as systems thinking and path dependency along with neoclassical analysis. Emphasizes sustainable development, not economic growth. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Sustainability.
ECON 3310.prereqs: ECON 1010 or ECON 1050 with a “C” or better or consent of instructor

ECON 3410.name: International Economics
ECON 3410.description: Analysis of the basis for and consequences of opening an economy to the international arena. Specific issues considered are the benefits and costs of international trade, the reason for barriers to trade, the determination of exchange rates and the effect of government policies of international good and factor flows.

ECON 3500.name: Economic History of the United States
ECON 3500.description: American economic organization and institutions and their development from colonial times to the present.

ECON 3510.name: Topics in Global Economic History
ECON 3510.description: This course and its variants explore the economic history of non-US regions, such as, but not limited to, Latin America, Europe, Africa and Asia, in a seminar setting. It is designed to be an application of micro and macroeconomic concepts.

ECON 3590.name: Globalization
ECON 3590.description: Globalization is studied as part of an exchange of technology, goods, and financial markets. The exchanges of goods, services, and ideas across national borders are pervasive. Communication systems help this process, but also help those who resist globalization to better articulate and organize their viewpoints. Approved for LAS Global Awareness requirement.

ECON 3690.name: Industrial Organization
ECON 3690.description: Examines the application of economic theory to business behavior, strategy, and market structure.
ECON 3690.prereqs: ECON 1010 or ECON 1050 with a “C” or better

ECON 3710.name: Comparative Economic Systems
ECON 3710.description: An examination of the underlying economic logic and relative advantages/disadvantages of differing economic systems. Special attention is paid to market-based economies, planned economies, Islamic economies, and shareholder economic systems. Approved for LAS Social Science area and Global Awareness requirements.

ECON 3720.name: East Asian Economic Growth
ECON 3720.description: The economic transformation of East Asia since the end of the Second World War brought unprecedented sustained economic growth to a significant share of the global population. This course explores the historical roots and methods of this transformation and explores the current challenges facing this region. Particular emphasis is given to the economies and economic transition of Japan, the Republic of Korea, and the People’s Republic of China.

ECON 3730.name: Economics of South Asia
ECON 3730.description: This course will provide students with an understanding of the how economic issues within South Asia have evolved in the post-colonial period. Topics include the role of the state in post-colonial economic development and a concern with industrialization, technical change and development of human capital; the impact of patron-client relationships on economic performance, agriculture and environment; globalization, economic reform and poverty and income inequality.

ECON 3770.name: Economic Development
ECON 3770.description: Explores the nature and sources of improvement in the standard of living in a nation or region. Among the issues addressed are the measurement of development, the role of government, gender implications of development, and environmental and economic sustainability. Local, regional, and international issues are addressed. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Sustainability.
ECON 3770.prereqs: ECON 1010 or ECON 2020 with a “C” or better

ECON 3800.name: The Economics of US Professional Sport
ECON 3800.description: The Investigation of the economics of professional US sport through presentation, lecture and Discussion.

ECON 3850.name: Law and Economics
ECON 3850.description: Examines how economic theory has been applied in legal theory and been used to shape legal outcomes. Numerous cases are examined.
ECON 3850.prereqs: ECON 1010 or ECON 1050 with a “C” or better

ECON 3870.name: Behavioral Economics
ECON 3870.description: Behavioral Economics explores the challenge to traditional models of economics offered by the work of economists and social scientists such as Daniel Kahneman. By exploring the role that social framing, personal psychology, and emotional responses play in economics decisions, the limits of traditional economic theory is explored and extensions to traditional theory considered.
ECON 3870.prereqs: ECON 1010 or ECON 1050 with a “C” or better

ECON 3980.name: Special Topics in Economics
ECON 3980.description: A study of special topics in economics. Topics vary from semester to semester and generally emphasize the application of economic analysis to current issues.

ECON 4010.name: Advanced Microeconomic Theory
ECON 4010.description: Study of the core of microeconomic theory using calculus. Topics include: consumer theory of the firm, profit maximization, efficiency and market failure. Several advanced topics from recent developments in microeconomics are also examined.
ECON 4010.prereqs: ECON 3010 with a “C” or better, and MATH 1120 or MATH 1350, or consent of instructor

ECON 4020.name: Advanced Macroeconomic Theory
ECON 4020.description: Study of the core of macroeconomic theory using calculus. Topics include Keynesian vs. Classical economic models, macroeconomic growth models, open economy macroeconomics, and macroeconomic policy analysis.
ECON 4020.prereqs: ECON 3020 with a “C” or better or consent of instructor

ECON 4250.name: Urban Economics
ECON 4250.description: Economic analysis of why cities exist, where they develop, how they grow, and how different activities are arranged within cities. Explores the economics of urban problems such as: poverty, congestion, pollution, and crime.
ECON 4250.prereqs: ECON 1010 or ECON 1050 with a “C” or better

ECON 4410.name: International Trade Policy
ECON 4410.description: Uses various models to analyze why countries trade, how and why they restrict trade, with a focus on US trade policy. Studies international trade agreement and disputes at bilateral and multilateral levels, with an emphasis on WTO.

ECON 4440.name: Decision and Game Theory
ECON 4440.description: An introduction to decision theory and game theory. No mathematical knowledge beyond high school algebra is assumed. Theoretical development of decision theory and game theory will be coupled with application of both to practice and the real world. See course schedule for topics covered.
ECON 4440.prereqs: ECON 1010 or PSC 3500 or PHIL 1120 or PHIL 3420

ECON 4500.name: Money and Banking
ECON 4500.description: The study of the interaction between financial markets and the Federal Reserve Banking system. Emphasizes the conduct of monetary policy to encourage economic growth and stability. Topics include interest rates, inflation, the money supply and the influence of these variables on the business cycle. Not available for credit to students who have completed FNCE 4500.

ECON 4510.name: Constitution and the Economy
ECON 4510.description: Considers the economic role of government expressed in the Constitution and in Supreme Court opinions. Emphasis is on liberty, efficiency, and prosperity. Special topics include: police power, takings, commerce clause, and substantive due process.

ECON 4520.name: Economic Freedom
ECON 4520.description: Examines the philosophy of individual liberty as a basis for the study of normative (or welfare) economics. The course considers theory, application, and critiques. Topics include: constitutional foundations, efficiency, spontaneous order, index of economic freedom, and contemporary policy issues.

ECON 4530.name: Power and Prosperity
ECON 4530.description: Uses three books by Mancur Olson to study the economic prosperity of nations. Considers whether Olson’s work presents a dynamic theory of political economy. Topics include: free rider behavior, economics of interest groups, rent seeking, and socially-contrived markets.

ECON 4810.name: Introduction to Econometrics
ECON 4810.description: Development and application of multiple regression techniques in testing economic theories.
ECON 4810.prereqs: ECON 3010 or ECON 3020, ECON 2810 with a “C” or better or consent of instructor

ECON 4990.name: Senior Seminar
ECON 4990.description: Required of all economics majors. This course provides an opportunity for economics majors to demonstrate the ability to access existing economic theory and evidence, apply existing theories and evidence to issues of current economic interest, and develop written assessments of issues of current economic interest in a seminar setting. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Summit.
ECON 4990.prereqs: ECON 2810, ECON 3010, and ECON 3020 with a “C” or better

EDUC 1000.name: Introduction to Inclusive Education
EDUC 1000.description: This course introduces the history, theoretical foundations, the law, and an introduction to programmatic designs to meet the broad range of needs of all young children. Includes 15 hours of fieldwork in local inclusive classrooms. Course typically offered: Fall, Spring

EDUC 2000.name: Intro to Educational Psychology
EDUC 2000.description: Provides teachers with the knowledge of psychology most relevant to teaching. The focus is on areas of child development and major learning theories and their application in the classroom.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                Course typically offered: Fall, Spring

EDUC 2100.name: Introduction to Technology in Education
EDUC 2100.description: This course explores the foundations, strategies, and tools for using technology as a means of engaging all students within inclusive educational settings. A focus is placed on universal design for learning (UDL) as a framework for selecting, evaluating, and implementing educational technology. Course typically offered: Fall, Spring

EDUC 2200.name: Children’s Literature
EDUC 2200.description: This course is an introduction to children’s literature. Students will read a variety of genres, explore issues related to children’s literature, and engage in a significant amount of responsive and evaluative writing. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity); Explore-Arts, Humanities, and Cultures; Writing Intensive. Course typically offered: Fall

EDUC 2300.name: Health and Physical Education for Educators
EDUC 2300.description: This course provides an overview of physical education and health standards, with specific attention to how they are addressed in the elementary school curriculum. Instructional strategies are explored for the integration of movement and health concepts into other content areas. Course typically offered: Spring

EDUC 2400.name: Arts Integration for Educators
EDUC 2400.description: This course will focus on methods and materials for teaching visual art and music as they relate to the growth and development of children. Emphasis will be on curriculum, methods, and strategies for prospective K-6 classroom teachers. Course typically offered: Spring

EDUC 2500.name: Integrated Social Studies I
EDUC 2500.description: This course will provide an overview of United States geography, history, political science, economics, sociology, and anthropology. The main goals of this course are to provide students with an understanding of past and current events in the United States through the lens of multiple social sciences and to increase awareness of the connection of past events to our current society.

EDUC 2600.name: Integrated Science I
EDUC 2600.description: This course introduces the exploration of major connecting themes in life sciences, earth science, and physical science. Concepts covered explore science topics through discussion, demonstrations, inquiry activities, hands-on laboratory activities, readings, and presentations. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Sustainability. Course typically offered: Fall

EDUC 2650.name: Integrated Science II
EDUC 2650.description: This course expands upon the major themes in  life sciences, earth science, and physical science introduced in IELM 2000. Concepts covered explore science topics through discussion, demonstrations, inquiry activities, hands-on laboratory activities, readings, and presentations. Course typically offered: Spring

EDUC 2700.name: Schools, Society, and Diversity
EDUC 2700.description: Emphasizing the foundations of American education through a contemporary lens, the course investigates multiple dimensions of diversity and society impacting today’s schools. Implications for innovative educational curricula and pedagogy are explored. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Society, Health and Behavior, and Writing Intensive. Course typically offered: Fall, Spring

EDUC 3800.name: English as a Second Language for Educators
EDUC 3800.description: Presents current and emerging philosophies, theories,and methods on teaching literacy and content areas to culturally and linguistically diverse students. Open to juniors/seniors only. Course typically offered: Spring

EDUC 3900.name: Early School Diversity Practicum
EDUC 3900.description: Provides early school diversity experiences for potential teachers in public school classrooms. This experience focuses on the roles, responsibilities and qualities of the professional teacher through practical experience. Open to juniors/seniors only. Can be repeated for up to 3 credits. Course typically offered: Fall

EDUC 3991.name: Introduction to Professional Year - Inclusive Early Childhood
EDUC 3991.description: All UCCS students wishing to enter the IECE Professional Year must submit a packet of request materials. This course also includes support professional self-reflection, resources for developing a professional resume and for passing the Praxis exams. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

EDUC 3992.name: Introduction to Professional Year - Elementary
EDUC 3992.description: All UCCS students wishing to enter the Elementary Professional Year must submit a packet of request materials. Materials will be submitted online via the campus LMS. Successful completion of this course is prerequisite to all other Professional Year course work and field work. Course typically offered: Spring

EDUC 3994.name: Introduction to Professional Year - Secondary
EDUC 3994.description: All UCCS students wishing to enter the Secondary Professional Year must submit a packet of request materials. Materials will be submitted online via the campus LMS. Successful completion of this course is prerequisite to all other Professional Year course work and field work. Course typically offered: Spring

EDUC 4100.name: Elementary Curriculum, Instruction, and Classroom Management
EDUC 4100.description: Principles of curriculum design, instructional models and practice, standards-based curriculum and assessment, planning, organization, and classroom management and discipline.

EDUC 4600.name: Secondary Classroom Management
EDUC 4600.description: This course will explore the importance of establishing a positive structured learning environment by developing a successful classroom management model, and will provide a comprehensive knowledge base concerning the two main strands of instructional and behavior management.

EDUC 4720.name: Teaching Reading and Writing in the Content Area
EDUC 4720.description: Designed to help secondary teachers become aware of the reading and writing process and how they apply to subject matter material. Emphasizes a framework for functionally teaching reading and writing within a particular content area and strategies for increasing student independence with print.

EDUC 4740.name: Differentiating Instruction for Secondary Teachers: Teaching to Meet the Needs of All Learners
EDUC 4740.description: Participants will build a foundation of understanding from which they will develop skills, strategies, and resources that they can then apply in their teaching to address the complex challenges of meeting the diverse learning needs of all students.

EDUC 4790.name: Secondary Curriculum, Instruction and Evaluation
EDUC 4790.description: Students develop an understanding of the context in which instruction takes place in today’s middle and high schools, as well as principles of curriculum design, including standards-based lesson and unit planning. Methods of assessment, interpretation of results, and diagnostic teaching will be addressed.

EDUC 4810.name: Secondary English Methods
EDUC 4810.description: Secondary English Methods gives an overview of instructional theory, methods, and materials in English and helps the students develop teaching strategies and address the Colorado model content standards.

EDUC 4840.name: Secondary Social Studies Methods
EDUC 4840.description: Secondary Social Studies Methods gives an overview of instructional theory, methods, and materials in social studies and helps students develop teaching strategies and address the Colorado model content standard.

EDUC 4850.name: Secondary World Languages Methods
EDUC 4850.description: Secondary World Languages Methods gives an overview of instructional theory, methods, and materials in World Languages and helps students develop teaching strategies and address the Colorado content standards.

EDUC 4900.name: School Experience - Secondary
EDUC 4900.description: Pre-student teaching field experience. Summer: Teaching in a summer program for area secondary schools. Fall: 8 weeks in a PDS middle school site and 8 weeks in a PDS high school site observing, assisting, teaching.

EDUC 4950.name: Secondary - Student Teaching
EDUC 4950.description: Secondary education students, in consultation with members of the school of education faculty, will be assigned to a secondary professional development school for full-day teaching for a period of sixteen weeks. During this time students will demonstrate, through direct experience, competency and understanding of the teaching-learning process. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Summit. Course typically offered: Spring

ECE 1000.name: Electrical & Computer Basics
ECE 1000.description: Foundational course intended for students with little to no technical background. Basic electrical circuit principles and concepts explored through hands-on projects. Also, basic computer design, operation and programming will be explored through hands-on projects. Does not count towards ECE major. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Physical and Natural World.

ECE 1001.name: Introduction to Robotics
ECE 1001.description: An introductory course in robotics integrating hardware and software. Students build robots with sensors & motors and write programs to control the robot. Students learn fundamental sequential C programming skills. Students use Arduino Robot kits to implement their designs. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Writing Intensive.
ECE 1001.prereqs: ECE majors should take ECE 1001 with Compass WI, non-ECE majors should take ECE 1002 w/out Compass WI, or permission of instructor

ECE 1002.name: Introduction to Robotics
ECE 1002.description: An introductory course in robotics integrating hardware and software. Students build robots with sensors & motors and write programs to control the robot. Students learn fundamental sequential C programming skills. Students use Arduino Robot kits to implement their designs.
ECE 1002.prereqs: ECE majors should take ECE 1001 with Compass WI, non-ECE majors should take ECE 1002 w/out Compass WI, or permission of instructor

ECE 1021.name: Computer-Based Modeling and Methods of Engineering
ECE 1021.description: Emphasis on algorithm development for solving engineering problems. Advanced topics in the C programming language: arrays, user functions, pointers, data structures, and file I/O.
ECE 1021.prereqs: ECE 1001 or ECE 1002, MATH 1320 or MATH 1350, College of Engineering students only

ECE 1411.name: Logic Circuits I
ECE 1411.description: Learn fundamentals of digital logic circuits, number systems, logic gates, and Boolean Algebra. Students will design combinational logic circuits.
ECE 1411.coreqs: ECE 1421 for Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering students

ECE 1421.name: Logic Circuits Laboratory I
ECE 1421.description: Through a series of laboratory sessions, students will design and build combinational logic circuits, gaining practical experience with discrete components.
ECE 1421.coreqs: ECE 1411 for Electrical Engineering and Computer Engineering students

ECE 2001.name: Intermediate Robotics Programming
ECE 2001.description: Continuation of ECE 1001/1002, with additional components and sensors, using more advanced topics in the C programming language; arrays, user functions, pointers, data structures and file I/O.
ECE 2001.prereqs: ECE 1001 or ECE 1002 or Permission of Instructor

ECE 2021.name: Computer Based Modeling in C
ECE 2021.description: Emphasis on algorithm development and H/W implementation of C programs for solving engineering problems. Students learn to write structured C programs using: arrays, user functions, pointers, data structures, file 1/0 and multi-file compiles.
ECE 2021.prereqs: ECE 1001 or ECE 1002 or Permission of Instructor

ECE 2050.name: Introduction to Physical Electronics
ECE 2050.description: Introduction to electronic device materials science. Topics include crystals, metals, alloys, insulators, semiconductors, conduction, quantum considerations. Ethical and professional issues with materials in the global, economic, environmental, and societal contexts are studied.

ECE 2205.name: Circuits and Systems I
ECE 2205.description: Modeling and analysis of analog circuits and linear systems. Kirchoff’s current and voltage laws. Uses time-domain methods and s-domain transfer functions to solve differential equations of first and second-order RLC circuits with op amps. Transient and steady-state response to steps and complex exponentials. Zero-input, zero-state, and initial-state response. Introduction to circuit simulation.

ECE 2210.name: Circuit Analysis I
ECE 2210.description: Modeling and analysis of electrical devices and circuits, including operational amplifiers. Transient and steady state response using classical differential equation methods. Impulse and step responses.

ECE 2411.name: Logic Circuits II
ECE 2411.description: Learn design and implement synchronous sequential logic circuits. Mealy and Moore machine, states assignment, state reduction and encoding. Verilog HDL as modeling and verifying tool for both combinational and sequential logic circuits in a series of laboratories.

ECE 2610.name: Introduction to Signals and Systems
ECE 2610.description: Mathematical representation of signals and systems; spectrum representation; representation of signals by sample values; discrete-time filter characterization and response; the z-transform; continuous-time signals and linear, time-invariant systems; frequency response; continuous-time Fourier transform and application to system analysis. MATLAB basics with application to signals and systems. Includes lectures,  demonstrations, and laboratory assignments.
ECE 2610.prereqs: MATH 1360 and (ECE 1021 or ECE 2021 or CS 2060) or instructor approval

ECE 3001.name: Electronic Projects
ECE 3001.description: Designed for non-engineering majors. In the Fall semester, the principles of “How We Communicate” are introduced through hands-on building and testing of radio circuits. In the Spring semester, the principles of “How We Control” are introduced through hands-on building, programming, and testing of micro-controllers. The history, personalities, social and cultural impacts, economic and business impacts, and sustainability issues are integrated into the lecture material for the target technology.

ECE 3003.name: Advanced Robotics
ECE 3003.description: Explore advanced robotics topics through the project management process. Project based class with scheduled milestones, min. lecture, max. applied. For the final project, each student will build and program a small autonomous vehicle to navigate between GPS coordinates.
ECE 3003.prereqs: ECE 2021 or DASE 2021 or Permission of Instructor

ECE 3005.name: C++ and GUI Programming
ECE 3005.description: A hands-on course in C++ programming and GUI development integrating hardware and software. Students implement programs on a Raspberry Pi with a Touchscreen. Basic computer architecture and the Linux OS are covered. Min. lecture, max. applied.
ECE 3005.prereqs: DASE 2021 or ECE 2021 or ECE 1021 or Permission of Instructor

ECE 3007.name: Python & Jupyter Programming
ECE 3007.description: A hands-on course in Python programming and Jupyter Notebook development using various add-on libraries; integrating hardware and software. Students implement programs on a Raspberry Pi with a touch screen. Basic computer architecture and the Linux OS are covered. Min. lecture, max. applied.
ECE 3007.prereqs: ECE 2021 or ECE 1021 or DASE 2021 or Permission of Instructor

ECE 3009.name: IoT on AWS
ECE 3009.description: A hands-on course in Amazon Web Services (AWS) Internet of Things (loT) programming; integrating hardware and software. Students initiate programs on a Raspberry Pi, through AWS, to different types of loT devices. Min. lecture, max. applied.
ECE 3009.prereqs: ECE 1021 or ECE 2021 or DASE 2021 or Permission of Instructor

ECE 3020.name: Semiconductor Devices I
ECE 3020.description: An introduction to semiconductor devices used in modern microelectronic technologies. The course objective is to provide an understanding of the fundamental physical principles and concepts underlying the operation and use of the most important semiconductor devices.
ECE 3020.prereqs: ECE 2050, and either ECE 2205 or ECE 2210

ECE 3110.name: Electromagnetic Fields I
ECE 3110.description: Static electric and magnetic field analysis, Poisson’s and Laplace’s equations, steady electric current, fields of steady electric currents, ferromagnetic materials, boundary-value problems for static fields, time-varying electric and magnetic fields, and Maxwell’s equations and wave equations. Relationship between field and circuit theory.

ECE 3120.name: Electromagnetic Fields II
ECE 3120.description: Electromagnetic wave propagation in dielectric and conducting media: solutions to the wave equations, transmission lines, waveguides and resonators, antennas and radiation, uniform and non-uniform plane waves. Design involving considerations of electromagnetic fields.

ECE 3201.name: Electronic Projects Lab
ECE 3201.description: Fall offering - operation, building, and testing radio projects. Spring offering - operation, building, and testing of uC projects.  College of Engineering students only.

ECE 3205.name: Circuits and Systems II
ECE 3205.description: Circuit analysis in the frequency domain. Phasors, sinusoidal steady-state response, and impedance, Fourier series/transforms and Laplace transforms. Design of active and passive analog filters. Includes lectures, demonstrations, and laboratory assignments.

ECE 3210.name: Electronics I
ECE 3210.description: Semiconductor device use in electronic circuits. Topics include amplifier theory, advanced op-­amp circuits, diode circuits and applications, MOS and BJT transistor operation, characteristics, basic transistor amplifiers.

ECE 3220.name: Electronics II
ECE 3220.description: Transistor power amplifiers, basic IC circuits, differential and multi-stage amplifier design, high-frequency models, frequency response, feedback, design of IC op-amps.

ECE 3230.name: Electronics Laboratory I
ECE 3230.description: Electronics test and measurement techniques including the use and limits of: power supplies, signal generators, multimeters, oscilloscopes, probes, automation. Op-amps and op-amp circuits, diodes, sensors, transistor characterization and amplifiers. Written reports emphasize results, issues.

ECE 3240.name: Electronics Laboratory II
ECE 3240.description: Amplifier design from theory, simulation, breadboard, through pcb design, build, solder and characterization. Advanced transistor amplifier build and characterization; single-stage, multi-stage, frequency response, feedback. Written reports emphasis on documenting results and issues.

ECE 3420.name: Microprocessor Systems Laboratory
ECE 3420.description: Introduction to microprocessor development systems and foundations of system design. Assembly language will be used in the development. Use of high-level languages will also be discussed.

ECE 3430.name: Introduction to Microcomputer Systems
ECE 3430.description: Design of microcomputer systems including assembly language programming and interfacing techniques. Emphasis is on the practical application of microcomputers as solutions to engineering problems.

ECE 3440.name: Microcomputer Systems Laboratory
ECE 3440.description: Experiments are performed to program and interface microcomputer systems to design and implement microcomputer-based systems. Emphasis is on the application of the microcomputer as a tool to solve control and data acquisition problems.

ECE 3510.name: Linear System Theory
ECE 3510.description: Characterization of linear systems by impulse response, convolution, transfer function. Linear differential equations and linear difference equations as models. Applications to circuits, electromechanical systems, etc. Transform methods include: Fourier series, Fourier transforms, and Laplace transforms. Introduction to state variables, and the state transition matrix. Use of a variety of models in design.

ECE 3610.name: Engineering Probability and Statistics
ECE 3610.description: An introduction to probability and statistics with application to solving engineering problems. Includes the axioms of probability, random variables, density functions, distributions functions, expectations. Gaussian random variables, bivariate random variables, sums of independent random variables. Estimation of sample mean and variance. Monte Carlo simulation, binomial, hypergeometric, Poisson counting processes, confidence intervals, reliability, failure rates, the Weibull model, the log-normal model, estimation using regression. Introduction to random processes. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Navigate; Writing Intensive.

ECE 3611.name: Engineering Probability and Statistics
ECE 3611.description: An introduction to probability and statistics with application to solving engineering problems. Equivalent to ECE 3610, but with no Compass requirements.

ECE 3910.name: Power Systems I
ECE 3910.description: Basic concepts and analytical methods in three-phase electric power systems: single-phase equivalent models; per-unit system of calculations; power, apparent power, and energy; basic properties of power systems elements; short-circuit current; voltage drop; and losses. Includes lectures and demonstrations.

ECE 4000.name: Electrical or Computer Engineering Internship
ECE 4000.description: Internship with company, non-profit, government or academic institutions with a minimum of 140 hrs for 3 credits. Requires prior agreement between direct supervisor and professor; documentation includes learning goals, schedules, and deliverables. Cannot be at a student’s regular work.

ECE 4020.name: Semiconductor Devices II
ECE 4020.description: Advanced study of the electrical and transport properties of semiconducting and solid state devices and integrated device structures. Topics include: pn junction device structures, non-ideal effects in small geometry Mosfets, compound semiconducting devices, CCDs, negative conductance microwave devices.

ECE 4040.name: Introductory VLSI Fabrication Laboratory
ECE 4040.description: Various types of VLSI fabrication processes such as thermal oxidation, rapid thermal annealing, diffusion, physical vapor deposition, ion implantation, photolithography and etching. In addition, students will use a variety of device characterization techniques available in the laboratory.

ECE 4050.name: Microelectronics IC Fabrication Laboratory
ECE 4050.description: Independent experimental project in which students are expected to acquire the theoretical understanding of modern IC fabrication process, perform the IC processing and supporting measurements, and write detailed laboratory reports. Students should take ECE 4050 before ECE 4896.

ECE 4070.name: Electronic Properties of Materials
ECE 4070.description: Principles and applications of the electrical, optical, magnetic, and thermal properties of engineering electronic materials. The treatment is designed for students specializing in the areas of microelectronics, solid state, and electromagnetics.

ECE 4080.name: VLSI Processing
ECE 4080.description: Introductory study of the various processes such as oxidation, diffusion, epitaxy, ion-implantation, photolithography, CVD, plasma processing, etc., used in contemporary fabrication of modern microelectronic technologies; use and understanding of process modeling programs used in design, fabrication, and simulation of MOSFET and bipolar microelectronics technologies.

ECE 4095.name: Nanotechnology I
ECE 4095.description: Application to advanced semiconductors and oxide electronics in which electron-electron interactions dictate device operations is the final goal of the series. Advanced device technology in the nanometer scale era and advances in strongly correlated electron devices need specialized knowledge in many areas of quantum physics which involve Non-Equilibrium Green’s Function (NEGF) formalism and advanced techniques of quantum field theory in condensed matter. Students pursuing MSEE and PhD programs are encouraged to have knowledge in these formalisms in order to conduct research in advanced areas of device physics. The treatment is essentially an engineering application of fundamental formalisms in practical applications. Only advanced undergraduates with an interest in MSEE and PhD in Physics or Electrical Engineering may take this course with instructor permission. Meets with ECE 5095.

ECE 4110.name: Electromagnetic Theory and Applications
ECE 4110.description: An intermediate level fields course beginning with the classical development of Maxwell’s equations and the Wave equation. Included are electrostatics, the steady magnetic field, plane-wave propagation, Poynting’s vector, guided waves, transmission lines, wave guides, the interaction of fields and matter, and concluding with an introduction to the subject of radiation. Dirac-delta and Dyadic Green’s function methods of problem solution are treated.

ECE 4120.name: Antenna Engineering
ECE 4120.description: Antenna engineering theory based on electromagnetic radiation is introduced. Various antennas including linear wire, aperture/horn, printed-circuit, and arrays are introduced. The design, fabrication, and measurement of antennas are covered. Prer. or

ECE 4150.name: Microwave Measurements Laboratory
ECE 4150.description: Experiments with transmission lines and waveguide systems. Infrared imaging of electromagnetic fields. Measurement of antenna fields. Exposure to equipment and techniques used in microwave measurements. Design of microwave circuits.

ECE 4160.name: Electric Machines Lab
ECE 4160.description: Laboratory experiments to identify electrical machines characteristics and performance.

ECE 4162.name: Electric Machines
ECE 4162.description: The course material covers transformers analysis and operation, steady-state and dynamic analysis of rotating machines, synchronous, DC machines and poly-phase induction motors.

ECE 4180.name: Advanced Microwave Measurement Laboratory
ECE 4180.description: Advanced study of microwave circuits, experiments, procedures, measurement techniques. Topics include Friis equation, cascade gain/noise, antenna directivity/gain, saturation, receiver design, antennas, ERP, near-far fields, thermal noise, and electronic warfare. Meets with ECE 5180.

ECE 4200.name: Advanced Digital Design Laboratory
ECE 4200.description: A design laboratory focusing on the design of digital systems in Verilog using the Digilent Spartan 3 FPGA prototyping board. A contemporary design environment consisting of the Xilinx ISE tool for implementation and ModelSim/QuestaSim for simulation will be utilized.

ECE 4211.name: Rapid Prototyping with FPGAs
ECE 4211.description: Field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) are an important part of the overall design flow for application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) because they offer the potential of allowing cheap hardware prototypes to be built to meet a narrow window of opportunity. They also offer novel, programmable architectures. This course will focus on the combined use of FPGAs and modern synthesis tools to develop rapid prototypes of ASICs. Includes a team project.

ECE 4220.name: Analog IC Design
ECE 4220.description: A fundamental analog circuit design course that establishes relationships between semiconductor device theory, semiconductor processing technologies and the electrical and functional performance requirements of modern analog integrated circuits. Includes design project.

ECE 4222.name: Deep Learning
ECE 4222.description: An introduction to deep learning. A range of topics will be covered from basic deep learning algorithms, architectures, for deep learning, and applications to problem domains.
ECE 4222.prereqs: ECE 1021, ECE 2021, and CS 2060 or instructor permission

ECE 4230.name: Analog Filter Design
ECE 4230.description: Theory, specification, design, and simulation of active and passive analog filters based on modern integrated circuit technology and VLSI Design I design philosophy.

ECE 4242.name: Advanced Digital Design Methodology
ECE 4242.description: Focuses on modern digital design practice using computer-based design tools and then considers key steps in a modern design flow, with particular attention to the use of behavioral models in hardware description languages as a stepping stone to combinational and sequential logic synthesis. The Verilog language will be presented, along with ancillary topics of functional verification, testbench generation, timing analysis, fault simulation, and design for testability. Design examples will include microcontrollers, finite state machines for datapath control, serial and parallel communication protocol controllers, and typical architectures of synchronous computational units.

ECE 4250.name: Microwave Circuit Design
ECE 4250.description: An introduction to the design and analysis of microwave circuits both passive and active. Topics include microwave circuit analysis, measurement methods, transmission line structures, material properties, lumped elements, discontinuities, terminations, attenuators, directional couplers, hybrids, power dividers, impedance transformers, filters, mixers, switches, phase shifters, and amplifiers.

ECE 4260.name: Mixed Signal IC Design
ECE 4260.description: Design of data converters, switch capacitor filters, high performance opamps, phase locked loops, oscillators.

ECE 4270.name: CMOS Radio Frequency Integrated Circuit Design
ECE 4270.description: CMOS based high Frequency amplifier design, s-parameters, voltage references, noise, low noise amplifier (LNA), mixers, RF power amplifiers, phaselocked loops, oscillators and synthesizers, transmitter and receiver architectures and RFID systems.

ECE 4280.name: Advanced Verification Methodology
ECE 4280.description: Verification of electronic systems consumes 70% of the development cycle. This course teaches students how to develop high-quality verification environments with SystemVerilog and how to use advanced verification techniques such as assertions and coverage for digital systems.

ECE 4300.name: Research In Advanced Topics In Engineering
ECE 4300.description: This course will enable conducting research in various advanced topics in engineering: e.g., embedded/digital systems (FPGA/ASIC); data analytics/mining; machine learning and AI; hardware cybersecurity; adaptive cognitive radio; embedded control systems. Includes a final project, proposal, etc.
ECE 4300.prereqs: ECE 4242/5252 or ECE 4211/5211 or ECE 4330/5330 or approval from the instructor

ECE 4320.name: Fault Detection & Design for Testability
ECE 4320.description: Stuck-at fault modeling. Test generation for combinational circuits-Boolean difference, D algorithm, PODEM, FAN, critical path. Fault dominance and equivalence. Test generation for synchronous sequential circuits. Cost functions used in test generation. Fault simulation. Basics of design for testability.

ECE 4330.name: Embedded Systems Design
ECE 4330.description: Introduction to embedded systems including real time fault-tolerant significance. Study the hardware and software techniques to designing embedded system, including study of various embedded operating systems, embedded controllers and digital signal processing hardware. Study existing embedded systems.
ECE 4330.prereqs: ECE 3430, CS 1450, or consent of instructor

ECE 4340.name: VLSI Circuit Design I
ECE 4340.description: Design considerations for MOS integrated circuits with an emphasis on CMOS technology and the relationships between semiconductor device theory, semiconductor processing technologies, and the electrical and functional performance requirements of modern digital IC circuits. Physical behavior of CMOS transistors and integrated circuits, CMOS processing technology, CMOS circuit and logic design, design rules and structured design methodology.

ECE 4480.name: Computer Architecture and Design
ECE 4480.description: The design of large digital systems with emphasis on the computer. Architectural alternatives, instruction set design, implementations including microprogramming, and actual examples are discussed. Performance tradeoffs.

ECE 4510.name: Feedback Control Systems
ECE 4510.description: Linear system modeling and dynamic response; stability root-locus and frequency-response analysis; root-locus and frequency-response feedback-control design using simple networks such as PID, lead, and lag controllers.
ECE 4510.prereqs: ECE 2205, ECE 3205, or consent of instructor

ECE 4520.name: Multivariable Control Systems I
ECE 4520.description: Introduction to modeling and analysis of systems in state-variable format. Linear transformation, controlability, observability, pole-placement control, and observer design are studied in depth. Introduction to the linear quadratic regulator problem.

ECE 4530.name: Control Systems Laboratory
ECE 4530.description: Experimental-based modeling, system identification, and control of a magnetic levitation system. Experiments with feedback control using Simulink, PID design, stability, root-locus analysis and design, feeback linearization, and pole-placement design.

ECE 4540.name: Digital Control Systems
ECE 4540.description: Digital emulation of analog controllers. The z-transform. Sampling and reconstruction. Discrete time and hybrid systems. Stability analysis and digital controller design. Digital filter structures and quantization effects. Adaptive inverse control.

ECE 4560.name: Digital Control Laboratory
ECE 4560.description: Discrete-time control systems will be designed and tested using microcomputers, compensators, A/D and D/A converters, and analog computers. Experiments in the control of discrete and analog systems will be performed.

ECE 4610.name: Analysis of Random Signals
ECE 4610.description: Probability and random variables. Practical aspects and methods for analyzing and interpreting random signals. Statistical and parametric descriptions, estimators and errors for measurement data.

ECE 4611.name: Physical-Layer Security
ECE 4611.description: The fundamentals of physical-layer security from first principles in information theory. Topics covered include equivocation, the wiretap channel, secrecy capacity, and signaling techniques for physical-layer security (e.g., beam forming, channel precoding, etc.).
ECE 4611.prereqs: ECE 3610 or ECE 3611; ECE 4645 or ECE 5645

ECE 4615.name: Statistical Signal Processing
ECE 4615.description: Concepts of signal processing using random signals, random vectors, random processes, signal modeling, Levinson recursion, Wiener filtering, spectrum estimation, and detection theory.
ECE 4615.prereqs: ECE 3610 or ECE 3611; ECE 4650 or ECE 5650

ECE 4625.name: Communication Systems I
ECE 4625.description: Introduction to principles of modern communication theory and signal processing: AM, FM, PAM, PCM, and delta modulation. Noise analysis, filtering, threshold effects, phase-locked loops, and introduction to digital modulation.

ECE 4630.name: Communications Systems II
ECE 4630.description: Continuation of ECE 4625. Digital modulation and demodulation; equalization and diversity; error correcting code performance in noise; introduction to spread spectrum and space communications; simulation of communication systems.
ECE 4630.prereqs: ECE 3610 or ECE 3611; ECE 4625 or ECE 5625

ECE 4645.name: Information Theory and Coding
ECE 4645.description: Information theory including entropy, mutual information, Markov chains, and channel capacity. Coding theory including block codes, convolutional codes, and an emphasis on modern coding techniques such as low-density parity-check codes.

ECE 4650.name: Modern Digital Signal Processing
ECE 4650.description: Study of linear discrete-time systems, linear difference equations, Z-transforms, discrete Fourier transform, fast Fourier transform, sensitivity, discrete random processes, quantization effects, and design-related concepts.

ECE 4655.name: Real-Time Digital Signal Processing
ECE 4655.description: An introduction into the design, development, and implementation of signal processing algorithms on real-time hardware targets. The emphasis will be on high-level language, but assembly language will also be discussed.
ECE 4655.prereqs: ECE 2610 or ECE 3205 or ECE 4650 or ECE 5650
