SOC 2225.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 2220, Communities in a Global Environment. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 2220.

SOC 2240.name: Childhood Socialization
SOC 2240.description: An examination of the process through which children define themselves as members of their culture. The influence of such “Cultural communicators” as the family, school, television, day care, children’s literature, games, toys and peer relations will be examined. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Society, Health and Behavior.

SOC 2250.name: Gendered Images
SOC 2250.description: Study of the images of women and men in American society, relating these stereotypes to actual conditions and experiences of women and men. Recommended to the returning student. Approved for LAS Social Science area and Cultural Diversity requirements. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity); Explore-Society, Health and Behavior. GT-SS3.

SOC 2260.name: Introduction to Environmental Sociology
SOC 2260.description: This course introduces the complex social, political and economic processes that define, create, and threaten our natural environment. Students explore various environmental and social problems from a sociological perspective and consider movements that (re)define our understanding of nature and sustainability. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity); Sustainability; Writing Intensive.

SOC 2300.name: Transitions in Adulthood: Lifecourse Perspectives
SOC 2300.description: This course will examine eight meaningful transitions that mark our entry into and journey through adulthood in American society. Additionally, we will supplement our understanding of these transitions by applying a cross-cultural perspective to each of them. In short, we will examine exactly what it means to be a “grown-up.” Approved for LAS Social Science area requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Society, Health and Behavior. Meets with GRNT 2300.

SOC 2400.name: Digital Society
SOC 2400.description: This class is an exploration of relationships with technology, new media, cyborgs, and futurism. Students will critically examine the meanings of digital ubiquity and connectivity and its ramifications on the social tapestry of the recent past, present, and future.

SOC 2500.name: Social Problems
SOC 2500.description: An introduction to the sociological perspective on social issues and problems such as deviance, race and ethnic relations, aging, crime and delinquency, war, drug abuse, alienation, mental illness, etc. Approved for LAS Social Science area requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Society, Health and Behavior.GT-SS3.

SOC 2505.name: Social Problems: Service Learning Component
SOC 2505.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 2500, Social Problems. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 2500.

SOC 2600.name: Intro to Social Psychology: Human Behavior in Interaction
SOC 2600.description: This course examines and applies Erving Goffman’s Dramaturgical Framework as a foundation on which to build a deeper understanding of interpersonal and social identities within the contexts of symbolic interaction, stigma, emotions, socio-pathology, trauma, and conformity.

SOC 2670.name: Sociology of Death and Dying
SOC 2670.description: Using biomedical, political, religious, and social science perspectives, this life-affirming course focuses on individual and societal attitudes and how they influence not only how and when we die, but also how we live and deal with the knowledge of death and loss.

SOC 3070.name: Social Research Methods
SOC 3070.description: An elementary examination of the various methods used in social research with emphasis on the scientific method and the role of empirical inquiry in sociology.
SOC 3070.prereqs: ENGL 1305, 1308, or 1310, sophomore status or higher, or consent of instructor

SOC 3150.name: Modern Sociological Theory
SOC 3150.description: A review of major sociological theorists of the 19th and 20th centuries. Will consider the major works of such pre-World War II writers as Karl Marx, Emile Durkheim, and Max Weber, and the post-war work of Foucault and others.
SOC 3150.prereqs: 9 hours of Sociology or consent instructor

SOC 3170.name: Social Statistics
SOC 3170.description: Course stresses quantitative techniques used in analyzing social data via the SPSS computer program. Research methodology is also emphasized. Satisfies the LAS and Compass Curriculum Quantitative and Qualitative Reasoning requirement as a statistics course when taken by a student who has either 1) successfully completed MATH 1040 (or a mathematics course that has college algebra as a prerequisite), OR 2) scored 87% or higher on the College Algebra placement test and scored 50% or higher on the Business Calculus placement test.

SOC 3210.name: American Minority Communities
SOC 3210.description: Examines the forces involved in shaping the development of ethnic minority communities in the United States. The course helps students understand contemporary minority communities via analyses of important historical moments, the unique cultures of each of the four large ethnic minorities, and social problems. While each community is examined independently of the others, interethnic relations are seen as important factors in the development of each community. Prer. SOC 1110 or Consent of Instructor.

SOC 3220.name: Urban and Community Sociology
SOC 3220.description: The city in terms of its social structure, residential and institutional patternings, processes of interaction, demographic processes and patterns of growth and change. Approved for LAS Cultural Diversity requirement.

SOC 3225.name: Urban and Community Sociology: Service Learning Component
SOC 3225.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 3220, Urban and Community Sociology. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 3220.

SOC 3230.name: Chicanx Communities
SOC 3230.description: Study of the origin, development, and current order of the Chicano community. Includes studies of the “Barrio,” ethnic  identity, social values, and the consequences of prejudice and discrimination. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity).

SOC 3235.name: Chicano Community: Service Learning Component
SOC 3235.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 3230, Chicano Community. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 3230.

SOC 3240.name: African American Communities
SOC 3240.description: Study of the origin, development, and contemporary nature of the black community. Encourages an understanding of black culture and values, and the consequences of prejudice and discrimination. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity).

SOC 3250.name: Power, Privilege and Social Difference
SOC 3250.description: Examines the processes and conditions that produce the systems of differences and privilege shaping our lived experiences. Critically analyzes the prevailing cultural ideologies surrounding class, race, gender, sexuality, and ability. Emphasizes awareness, respect, justice and resolution. Approved for LAS Cultural Diversity requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity).

SOC 3255.name: Power, Privilege, and Social Difference:  Service Learning Component
SOC 3255.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 3250, Power, Privilege, and Social Difference. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 3250.

SOC 3270.name: Global Indigenous Issues
SOC 3270.description: Examines the development and current nature of indigenous populations world-wide, with in-depth analyses of Native America. Includes issues of social structure, collective identity, cultural survival, and access to resources. Also examines consequences of public policy and development policy. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Explore-Society, Health and Behavior; Inclusiveness; Sustainability.

SOC 3280.name: Asian American Communities
SOC 3280.description: This course provides an intersectional overview of Asian American communities, identities, and issues from historical and contemporary perspectives. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity).

SOC 3290.name: Perspectives on Race and Ethnic Relations
SOC 3290.description: A survey of racism, discrimination, prejudice, and relationships between dominant and minority groups in selected areas of the world. Approved for LAS Cultural Diversity requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity).

SOC 3295.name: Perspectives on Race and Ethnic Relations: Service Learning Component
SOC 3295.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 3290, Perspectives on Race and Ethnic Relations. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 3290.

SOC 3300.name: Sport and Society
SOC 3300.description: Analysis of sport and its place in the culture life of contemporary societies. Focus on how sport and sport experiences are related to social development, social relations and major spheres of social life such as the economy, political order, education and religion.

SOC 3310.name: Sociology of the Family
SOC 3310.description: The family as a social institution. Historical development and contemporary cross-cultural analysis with emphasis on the contemporary American family.

SOC 3320.name: African American Families
SOC 3320.description: Examines the various manifestations of “Family” within the African American community and highlights the historical and contemporary structural forces which contributed to these shifting arrangements. Emphasis is also placed on gender and class variations in black family experiences.

SOC 3330.name: Restorative Dialogue
SOC 3330.description: Restorative practices are used in our judicial system, schools, and the work place. This highly interactive course will focus on the fundamental principles and practices of restorative justice (a victim-centered response to harm) and restorative dialogue (conflict conversation skills).
SOC 3330.prereqs: SOC 1400 or WEST 1400 or CJ 1003; or the GPS 1010 section, Peacebuilders

SOC 3340.name: Food, Health, and Inequality
SOC 3340.description: An introduction to the intersecting areas of food, culture, community, politics, economics, and health.  Power dynamics and social structures will be used to examine the risks of hunger, negative health outcomes, and cultural survival.  Approved for LAS Social Science area and Global Awareness requirements. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Sustainability; Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity); Explore-Society, Health and Behavior. Course typically offered: Rarely Offered

SOC 3345.name: Food, Health, and Inequality: Service Learning Component
SOC 3345.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 3340, Food, Health, and Inequality. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 3340.

SOC 3350.name: Sociology of Health and Illness
SOC 3350.description: This course examines the sociological dimensions of health and illness - how health issues are culturally framed; the impact of social position including race, class, and gender; and the social organization and power dynamics of health and healthcare institutions.

SOC 3360.name: Sociology of Drugs and Addiction
SOC 3360.description: Examines the sociological causes and consequences of drug addiction within historical, cultural, and social contexts. Assesses public policy approaches, treatment and social control.

SOC 3400.name: Criminology
SOC 3400.description: A critical introduction to the study of crime in the U.S. Includes the measurement of crime, nature and development of law, theories of causation, delinquency, and issues of differential treatment and disparities in the courts, corrections and by law enforcement. Approach is multidisciplinary. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity). Meets with WEST 3470.

SOC 3405.name: Criminology: Service Learning Component
SOC 3405.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 3400, Criminology. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 3400.

SOC 3410.name: Sociology of Law
SOC 3410.description: Emphasis is on the sociology of law, and the influence of the media on perceptions of the legal system. The criminal justice system is analyzed principally from the sociological viewpoint.

SOC 3440.name: Community Leadership
SOC 3440.description: This course profiles America’s democratic and civil rights history, current events, and leadership theory to demonstrate how community and collaboration among citizens have always been core to social change. Leadership will be examined as a personal calling and social responsibility.

SOC 3495.name: Youth Gangs: Service Learning Component
SOC 3495.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 3490, Youth Gangs. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 3490.

SOC 3570.name: Field Experience in Sociology
SOC 3570.description: Opportunity to obtain academic credit for directed learning in an ongoing social organization. The experience may be paid or volunteer. It is the principle responsibility of the student to obtain access to an appropriate placement. One hour of credit may be earned for each three hours a week of experience, up to a maximum of three credit hours.  Meets with WEST 3660.

SOC 3630.name: Adoption from the Inside Out: Sociological-Psychological Perspectives on Adoption
SOC 3630.description: Explores the practice of adoption through sociological and psychological lenses. Relinquishment and the adoption process in the U.S. and internationally are examined with consideration of how gender, sexuality, race, class, age, and disability intersect with political, economic, and religious institutional structures. Approved for LAS Cultural Diversity and Social Science area requirements. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Explore-Society, Health and Behavior; Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity).

SOC 3640.name: Sociology of Popular Culture
SOC 3640.description: Survey of critical approaches to leisure popular culture. Specific topics may include advertising, television, music, sport, subcultures and the body in popular culture.

SOC 4010.name: Special Topics in Sociology
SOC 4010.description: Offered to allow intensive study in a specific area on a “Demand” basis.  Meets with SOC 5010.

SOC 4040.name: Sociology of Gender and Sexuality
SOC 4040.description: This course will undertake a critical examination of the role of sex, gender, and sexuality in modern society. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity). Meets with WEST 4040.

SOC 4050.name: State and Society
SOC 4050.description: Explores the ways in which states are socially constructed and maintained via relationships of power, inequality, and other social mechanisms. Examines the reflexive relationship between the state and society and how both influence our social life.
SOC 4050.prereqs: SOC 1110 or 2050 or Consent of Instructor

SOC 4080.name: Men and Masculinities
SOC 4080.description: This class explores men as gendered beings and understands manhood as a social construct. Provides an overview of theories of manhood and topics including power and patriarchy; race, class and sexuality; men in families; work; violence; health; friendship and intimacy. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity).

SOC 4090.name: Research Practicum
SOC 4090.description: Practical experience in application and principles of research design and data processing to a social research problem selected by instructor.

SOC 4110.name: Sociology of Homelessness
SOC 4110.description: Examines the social, political, and economic dimensions of homelessness.  Emphasis on the extent, nature and causes of, and societal responses to, homelessness.  The course is grounded in a service-learning format, which involves working with homeless service and advocacy organizations.

SOC 4115.name: Sociology of Homelessness: Service Learning Component
SOC 4115.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 4110, Sociology of Homelessness. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 4110.

SOC 4120.name: Body, Power and Culture
SOC 4120.description: Introduces the sociological study of the human body through the intersectional lenses of disability, culture, gender, medicine, and beauty norms. Together, we will attempt to answer the question: “What is a ‘normal’ body, and who decides?”

SOC 4150.name: Contemporary Social Theory
SOC 4150.description: Focus on 20th and 21st sociological theory, with special attention on the production of sociological knowledge and new trends in theory, such as feminist theory, Marxism, postcolonial theory, Indigenous decolonial theory, and critical race theory.

SOC 4170.name: Advanced Statistics and Methods
SOC 4170.description: Designed to prepare students with advanced statistical techniques including multivariate linear regression and regression diagnostic, generalized linear models, survival analysis, as well as models for panel and hierarchical data. This course uses Stata to analyze large-scale survey data.

SOC 4180.name: Community Organization and Analysis
SOC 4180.description: Study of community variables; economic, cultural, political and social. Comparative analysis of race, class, gender, and ethnicity in community settings and review of a range of research methods.
SOC 4180.prereqs: A minimum of 60 credit hours completed or consent of instructor

SOC 4190.name: Deviant Behavior
SOC 4190.description: An examination of the definition, nature, perspectives and theories, consequences, and social control of deviant behavior. Various forms of problematic deviant behavior will be examined such as drug abuse, alcoholism, mental illness, suicide, and crime.

SOC 4195.name: Deviant Behavior: Service Learning Component
SOC 4195.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 4190, Deviant Behavior. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 4190.

SOC 4200.name: Sociology of Poverty
SOC 4200.description: Consideration of structural origins of poverty; the underclass and the dual economy. Analysis and evaluation of consequences of poverty, especially in relation to family, children, and career. Review of antipoverty programs. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity). Meets with WEST 4200.

SOC 4205.name: Sociology of Poverty: Service Learning Component
SOC 4205.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 4200, Sociology of Poverty. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 4200.

SOC 4210.name: Social Services and Welfare Reform
SOC 4210.description: Provides a sociological examination of the transformation of social welfare within both the United States and other industrialized nations. Emphasis is placed on the structural forces producing welfare reform, the strategies employed to achieve it, and the differential impact of this reform by race and gender. Open only to junior/senior/grad level.

SOC 4215.name: Social Services and Welfare Reform: Service Learning Component
SOC 4215.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 4210, Social Services and Welfare Reform. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 4210.

SOC 4220.name: Sustainable Urban Development
SOC 4220.description: Study of theories and practical applications of sustainable urban development at the local, regional, national, and international levels. Focuses on the sociological dimensions of urban sustainability including social, racial and regional inequalities, power structures, and ideology. Course emphasizes fieldwork and collaborative learning in local settings.

SOC 4225.name: Sustainable Urban Development: Service Learning Component
SOC 4225.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 4220, Sustainable Urban Development. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 4220.

SOC 4230.name: Foundations of Disability Studies
SOC 4230.description: A survey of the interdisciplinary field of disability studies. Course will cover: key concepts in disability studies, the history of people with disabilities, media representations of people with disabilities, bioethical issues involving people with disabilities, and disability culture.

SOC 4240.name: Sociology of Dis/Ability
SOC 4240.description: Assumes a sociological perspective to critically deconstruct traditional and medical interpretations of the meaning of disability. Focuses on the historical and cultural conditions that have produced the condition of disability and how disability intersects with gender, race, class, and sexuality. Approved for LAS cultural diversity requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity).
SOC 4240.prereqs: 9 hours of sociology or consent of instructor

SOC 4245.name: Sociology of Dis/Ability: Service Learning Component
SOC 4245.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 4240, Sociology of Dis/Ability. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 4240.

SOC 4250.name: Sociology of the Environment
SOC 4250.description: Examines how local and global environmental issues intersect with social dynamics of global inequality, poverty, gender, race and religion. Students explore how social activism empowers individuals to fight against corporate and governmental institutional processes affecting the environment. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Sustainability.

SOC 4290.name: Sport, Film, and Society
SOC 4290.description: This course takes a sociological and intersectional approach to sport film. We will watch films to understand how sports and athletes have been imagined in popular culture. Themes will include representation of race, class, gender, and sexuality; authoritarianism versus egalitarianism; and sportsmanship versus commercialism. Approved for LAS Cultural Diversity area requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity).

SOC 4300.name: Sociology of Sport
SOC 4300.description: Advanced analysis of sport from a sociological perspective. This course studies sport as social phenomena, structural relations, and a field of experience that has developed over time. Theoretical perspectives include Marxism, critical race theory, feminist theory, post-structuralism, and figuration theory. Meets with SL 5000, SOC 5300 and WEST 4300.

SOC 4310.name: Class, Stratification and Power
SOC 4310.description: Critical analysis of the theories and research on socioeconomic class and the reproduction of privilege, with a focus on the American class system. Addresses the prevailing cultural ideologies surrounding class as well as the ways in which class intersects with race, gender and disability.

SOC 4320.name: Religion in Society
SOC 4320.description: Examination of religion as a social and cultural institution; impacts for communities and for society; shaping of religious identities, values, and practices; the role of religion in social control, social conflicts, and social change. Meets with SOC 5330.
SOC 4320.prereqs: 6 hours of Sociology or consent of instructor

SOC 4330.name: Sociology of Education
SOC 4330.description: Analysis of the school as a social organization. Among the topics considered are power and control in the school; classroom organization and procedures and their relation to learning and personality development in children; role of educators; and reciprocal relations of school and community.

SOC 4360.name: Sociology of Media and Popular Culture
SOC 4360.description: This course introduces students to the interdisciplinary field of media studies. It takes a critical social science perspective but also draws on cultural theory and history. The goal is to critically interrogate a large part of contemporary life.

SOC 4370.name: Technology, Media, and Society
SOC 4370.description: A description and analysis of changing social structures and social relationships as a response to technological innovation and change. Emphasis also given to the role of technology in the development of selected countries outside the United States.

SOC 4380.name: Globalization and Development
SOC 4380.description: This course provides a multi-level examination of globalization, investigating the forces that influence this phenomenon and their effects on people, societies, and the world at large. Approved for LAS Global Awareness requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity); Sustainability; Writing Intensive.

SOC 4385.name: Globalization and Development: Service Learning Component
SOC 4385.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 4380, Globalization and Development. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 4380.

SOC 4400.name: Contemporary Social Movements
SOC 4400.description: Examination of the impact of social movements on the political, social and cultural practices of contemporary society. The course includes a brief review of the ‘movement politics’ of the 1960’s, contrasts these to the labor movement and other historical predecessors, with major attention devoted to the infusion of social movement practices and technology into the ‘mainstream’ structures of power and organization. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity).
SOC 4400.prereqs: SOC 1110 or SOC 2500; must have completed 60 credits

SOC 4420.name: Nonprofit and Nongovernmental Organizations
SOC 4420.description: This course examines nonprofit organizations (NPOs) and civil society in the United States by exploring the contributions to the social, political, and economic dimensions of society. It also analyzes the efficacy of nongovernmental organizations (NGOs) in an international context. Meets with SOC 5420. Approved for LAS Global Awareness requirement.

SOC 4430.name: Social Work Practice with Individuals and Families
SOC 4430.description: Public welfare services including problems involved in reconstructing personalities and improving relationships between them; the scope of social case work; and social worker as visiting teacher, family case worker, and investigator in other fields.

SOC 4450.name: Global Field Experience in Sociology
SOC 4450.description: Students develop sociological and interdisciplinary competencies through travel, academic assignments and structured field experience in globalized communities. Alternating topics/locations emphasize how academic knowledge informs real-world endeavors. Includes additional non-tuition costs. May be repeated once with different topic or location. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Navigate. Meets with SOC 5450.

SOC 4460.name: Field Studies in Sociology
SOC 4460.description: Field based investigation of specific aspects of society, communities or social contexts. Topic and credit vary.

SOC 4470.name: Travel Course: Intersections of Privilege
SOC 4470.description: Hybrid/travel course built around the White Privilege Conference, designed to provide foundational knowledge; extend and maximize learning; provide an opportunity to connect the WPC experience with research and best practices in the field; and to apply knowledge gained there.  Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity). Meets with WEST 2470/4470. Course typically offered: Spring

SOC 4480.name: Racial Storytelling: Montgomery Travel Course
SOC 4480.description: This hybrid travel course to Montgomery, Alabama uses an interdisciplinary exploration of the ways in which racial history and reality are constructed and given meaning through storytelling and narrative, and the ways in which relations of power imbue these narratives. Approved for LAS Cultural Diversity area requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity); Navigate. Meets with SOC 5480 and WEST 4480.

SOC 4490.name: Sociology Internship
SOC 4490.description: Students will be involved in community and organizational settings where they will gain practical work and networking experience. They will apply critical analysis, social theory, and research methods to their sites for their academic component.
SOC 4490.prereqs: Junior or Senior standing, consent of instructor required

SOC 4510.name: Community Development Field Work
SOC 4510.description: Students will be involved in community settings and learn to identify issues in terms of causes and develop proposals of action that might enhance community organization and structure.  Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

SOC 4520.name: Sociology of Corrections and Rehabilitation
SOC 4520.description: Examines the history of incarceration and corrections and provides a critical analysis of incarceration policies. Drawing on carceral studies and an intersectional approach, focuses on individuals’ lived experiences and group behavior in correctional facilities. Explores the reentry process and factors.

SOC 4530.name: Advanced Privilege Studies
SOC 4530.description: This course focuses on the issue of privilege through a historical and intersectional framework, examining race, gender, dis/ability, sexuality, and other social identities. Students will conduct their own research during this class. Approved for LAS Cultural Diversity requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Writing Intensive. Meets with WEST 4530.
SOC 4530.prereqs: SOC 1110 or WEST 1010 or consent of instructor

SOC 4550.name: Ethnography of Sport
SOC 4550.description: This course will focus on how sports produce worlds that are fundamentally focused on the human body. It is this focus that will allow us to investigate cultural forms that exist in practice without necessarily existing in language.

SOC 4560.name: Internship in Applied Sociology
SOC 4560.description: Participate in supervised activities in a structured program to facilitate learning in conjunction with concurrent cognate course. One hour class time per week plus 3 hours internship for each one hour of credit.
SOC 4560.prereqs: Sociology majors only, consent of instructor

SOC 4580.name: Sociology of Disasters
SOC 4580.description: Vulnerability to “natural” disasters is directly linked to social constructions, social inequalities, and economic, political, and cultural power structures. This course examines the ways in which disasters expose, challenge, or reinforce these dimensions. Approved for LAS Global Awareness area requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Sustainability; Inclusiveness.

SOC 4590.name: Youth Gangs
SOC 4590.description: A sociological examination of youth gangs. Factors related to formation and maintenance of youth deviant culture in different historical periods. The social construction of gangs, gang resistance to social control, and criminalization of youth of color. Structural, community and neighborhood influences. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity). Meets with WEST 3490.
SOC 4590.prereqs: A minimum of 60 credit hours completed or consent of instructor

SOC 4600.name: Critical Analysis of Capitalism
SOC 4600.description: Focus on the global operation of capitalism as an economic and social system. We study the global flows of capital and how the logic of capital unfolds throughout the world and its impact on everyday life. Approved for LAS Global Awareness requirement.
SOC 4600.prereqs: Minimum of 60 credit hours completed including SOC 3150 or SOC 3250

SOC 4610.name: Youth and Society
SOC 4610.description: Explore diverse sociological issues related to youth, focusing on adolescence, young adulthood, and social inequalities (e.g.,  class, gender, sexuality, and race). The course will also consider various aspects of youth culture, including risk-taking, social media/digital, and health.
SOC 4610.prereqs: 6 Hours of sociology or consent instructor

SOC 4650.name: Sociology of Mental Illness: Mad Studies
SOC 4650.description: A mad studies perspective on the nature, history, theories, and social control of “mental illness”. Societal factors related to the prevalence and labeling of mental illness, mental hospital patient/survivor experiences, mad pride social movements, and public policies will be examined.

SOC 4660.name: Sociology of Medicine
SOC 4660.description: Explores the social and cultural construction of medicine, medical practice, and disease across diverse cultures. Focuses on the medical systems of the the U.S. and other countries. Approved for LAS Global Awareness requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Inclusiveness; Sustainability.
SOC 4660.prereqs: Minimum of 60 credits or consent of instructor

SOC 4680.name: Inequality USA
SOC 4680.description: This course identifies how inequality is defined, measured, studied, and understood by geographers. Students will analyze quantitative and qualitative data sources to explain inequality in the U.S., and will conduct research identifying spaces of inequality in Colorado Springs. Approved for LAS Cultural Diversity requirement. Meets with SOC 5680, WEST 4680, GES 4680, GES 5680.

SOC 4700.name: Global Feminisms
SOC 4700.description: Identifies broad trends and changes in feminist interpretations and approaches to sexual politics, race, migration, religion, geopolitics, and globalization. A global look at women’s oppression and strategies of resisting subordination through various transnational feminist praxis, theory, and case studies. Approved for LAS Global Awareness requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity); Explore-Society, Health and Behavior.

SOC 4758.name: Sociology Capstone Course
SOC 4758.description: One-credit add-on course open to Sociology students to conduct primary research to meet the capstone requirement. The sociology senior capstone course is designed for sociology majors to demonstrate their cumulative learning of sociological theory, research methods, and substantive concepts and topics in the discipline.
SOC 4758.prereqs: SOC 3070, SOC 3150, and a minimum of 90 credits completed or consent of the instructor

SOC 4780.name: Global Migration
SOC 4780.description: This course examines contemporary human migration at a global scale. Drawing from works on world systems, transnationalism, and immigrant assimilation, among others, we will explore how social science perspectives on human mobility can expand our understandings of place, citizenship, and borders. Meets with SOC 5780, WEST 4780, GES 4780/5780.

SOC 4785.name: Sociology Capstone Course
SOC 4785.description: One-credit add-on course open to Sociology students to conduct primary research to meet the capstone requirement. The sociology senior capstone course is designed for sociology majors to demonstrate their cumulative learning of sociological theory, research methods, and substantive concepts and topics in the discipline. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Summit.
SOC 4785.prereqs: SOC 3070, SOC 3150, and a minimum of 90 credits completed or consent of the instructor

SOC 4960.name: Juvenile Delinquency
SOC 4960.description: Critical social science inquiry and sociological theories are used to examine youth crime in modem U.S. society. Studies structural inequalities and social differences in relationship to youth criminalization and disparities in the juvenile justice system. Explores youth gangs, drug use, policing and violence. Meets with SOC 5960 and WEST 4960. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity).
SOC 4960.prereqs: A minimum of 60 credit hours completed or consent of instructor

SOC 4965.name: Juvenile Delinquency: Service Learning Component
SOC 4965.description: This service-learning component is taken in conjunction with SOC 4960, Juvenile Delinquency. The student must volunteer as an intern in a community organization related to the substantive content of SOC 4960.

SOC 4980.name: Capstone Preparatory
SOC 4980.description: This course prepares students to complete a capstone research project in the subsequent semester. Students will: commit to specific research questions and methodological design, have one-on-one meetings with instructor for project feedback and approval, and complete all IRB requirements.

SOC 4990.name: The Sociology Capstone
SOC 4990.description: The sociology senior capstone course is designed for sociology majors as a tool to demonstrate their cumulative learning of sociological theory, research methods, and substantive concepts and topics in the discipline. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Summit.

SPAN 1010.name: Beginning Spanish I
SPAN 1010.description: Essentials of Spanish, oral-aural skills stressed with additional reading, writing, and grammar. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Arts, Humanities, and Cultures.

SPAN 1020.name: Beginning Spanish II
SPAN 1020.description: Essentials of Spanish continued. Additional oral-aural skills practice with increased grammar, reading, and writing. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Arts, Humanities, and Cultures.

SPAN 2110.name: Intermediate Spanish I
SPAN 2110.description: Spanish at the intermediate level with concentration on conversation, grammar, vocabulary, culture, and civilization or literature at that level. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Arts, Humanities, and Cultures.

SPAN 2111.name: Professional Span II-Intermediate Spanish for Professionals
SPAN 2111.description: This course is designed for students and professionals with some previous Spanish language background who want to use Spanish in a professional setting, as well as anyone wanting to travel or study in a Spanish-speaking country. The language and culture topics focus on practical situations that will lead to a A2 or B1 level certification and allow a student or professional to thrive in a Spanish-speaking environment. Students who intend to register for this class must have completed beginning Spanish classes 1 and 2.

SPAN 2120.name: Intermediate Spanish II
SPAN 2120.description: An intermediate Spanish course continuing conversational usage and cultural integration utilizing contemporary materials, newspapers, etc. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Arts, Humanities, and Cultures.

SPAN 2130.name: Applied Conversation
SPAN 2130.description: Conversation at the intermediate level on contemporary topics in Spanish culture.

SPAN 2920.name: Spanish for Health Professionals
SPAN 2920.description: The vocabulary and usage of the world of health care.  Applied language and cultural values of Latino cultures.

SPAN 2930.name: Business Spanish
SPAN 2930.description: The vocabulary and usage of the world of finance and commerce. Applied business correspondence, marketing and accounting terminologies.

SPAN 3000.name: Spanish Grammar and Composition
SPAN 3000.description: Designed to review extensively the functional application of modern Spanish. Presents a skill-development approach featuring graded compositions and oral practice based on material encountered in informal situations. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Writing Intensive.

SPAN 3007.name: Introduction to Cybersecurity in the Hispanic World
SPAN 3007.description: This advanced language course provides an introduction to technical Spanish and cultural issues associated with the field of cybersecurity in the Spanish-speaking world. Participants will learn to understand and communicate in Spanish issues related to cybersecurity in a culturally-focused environment, developing skills needed to understand the basic mechanisms at play in the field from a linguistic and cultural perspective.
SPAN 3007.prereqs: SPAN 2120 or equivalency or instructor permission

SPAN 3010.name: Advanced Spanish Conversation and Composition
SPAN 3010.description: Practice in conversation and development of skills in composition with emphasis in oral presentations and formal compositions, including academic essays. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Writing Intensive.

SPAN 3070.name: Sustainability in the Spanish Speaking World
SPAN 3070.description: Increase your understanding of the Spanish speaking natural and urban environments and issues of sustainability in Spain and the Spanish speaking world, as well as locally, through the study of media, resources, literature, and interaction with others and your community. Approved for the Compass Curriculum requirement: Sustainability and Writing Intensive.

SPAN 3100.name: Literary Analysis
SPAN 3100.description: Students read different genres - narrative, essay, short story, drama and poetry to facilitate the acquisition of critical skills in the identification of basic ideological and formalistic issues within texts being studied. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Inclusiveness.

SPAN 3190.name: Survey of Spanish Peninsular Literature
SPAN 3190.description: Introduction to literary form and expression through selected masterpieces of Peninsular literatures. Course is only offered one semester per year, generally in the spring.

SPAN 3200.name: Survey of Latin American Literature
SPAN 3200.description: Introduction to literary form and expression through selected masterpieces of Latin American literatures.  Course is only offered one semester per year, generally in the fall.

SPAN 3230.name: Applied Conversation
SPAN 3230.description: Conversation at the advanced level on contemporary topics in Spanish culture.

SPAN 3250.name: Hispanic Culture Studies
SPAN 3250.description: Cultural history of Spain. Readings of selected masterworks with discussion about art, music, architecture, folklore, and customs. Taught in Spanish. Course is only offered one semester per year, generally in the fall.

SPAN 3350.name: Spanish for Heritage Speakers
SPAN 3350.description: Designed for heritage speakers of Spanish or other linguistically qualified students. Emphasis is placed in the use of grammar and challenges particular to Heritage speakers such as orthography, inappropriate mix of English and Spanish, contrasts between standard Spanish and regional variations.
SPAN 3350.prereqs: Spanish speaking fluency or native or near native or SPAN 3000 or SPAN 3010 or permission of instructor

SPAN 3370.name: The Latin American Essay
SPAN 3370.description: Readings from essay. Writings from the conquest to contemporary society including Las Casas, Sarmiento, Hostos, Sierra, Gonzalez, Prada, Rodo, Paz.

SPAN 3490.name: Internship in Applied Spanish
SPAN 3490.description: The Language and Culture department will offer to advanced language students the opportunity to apply their knowledge in settings such as schools, social support agencies, etc. May be repeated up to three times for credit.

SPAN 3690.name: Hispanic Culture Through Film
SPAN 3690.description: The cinematic manifestations of the richness and the variety of Hispanic culture as expressed through an artistic and humanistic vision. May be repeated once provided the topic is different. Approved for LAS Humanities area requirement and Global Awareness requirement. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirements: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity); Explore-Arts, Humanities, and Cultures.

SPAN 3910.name: Spanish Theatre
SPAN 3910.description: A theatre practicum in Spanish stressing proper diction, articulation, and pronunciation as well as active involvement in public presentation of selected dramatic writers.

SPAN 3920.name: Advanced Spanish for Health Care
SPAN 3920.description: Advanced study of the vocabulary, language and cultural values of Latino cultures for the health care professional.

SPAN 3930.name: Advanced Business Spanish
SPAN 3930.description: Advanced study of the vocabulary and usage of the world of business and commerce.

SPAN 4010.name: Advanced Spanish Communication I
SPAN 4010.description: Designed to improve written expression Spanish. Detailed study of the nuances of grammar. Attention given to points most difficult for students, to composition skills, and to various styles of written Spanish.

SPAN 4110.name: Women in Hispanic Culture
SPAN 4110.description: Women’s contributions to various aspects of cultural production in the Spanish-speaking world (visual arts, film, literature) in historical context. Taught in English. May be included as part of Women’s Studies program.

SPAN 4150.name: Masterpieces of Spanish-Language Literature
SPAN 4150.description: Masterworks of major Spanish artists: readings and discussions.

SPAN 4210.name: Hispanic Heritage of Colorado
SPAN 4210.description: The study of the history and traditions of Hispanics in the state from the 16th century to the present. Approved for LAS Humanities area requirement and Cultural Diversity requirement. Meets with FCS 4210.

SPAN 4250.name: The Cultural Heritage in Latin America
SPAN 4250.description: The historical, cultural and political currents in Latin America beginning with Pre-Colombian indigenous cultures and continuing to the present.

SPAN 4253.name: Almodovar
SPAN 4253.description: Course focuses on the evolution of the films of Spanish filmaker Pedro Almodovar. The manner in which this innovative auteur has treated a variety of conceptual and formal issues will be examined, as will his vision of the cultural and social transformation of Spanish society from the early 1980s to the present. Meets with FILM 4253 and FCS 4253.

SPAN 4280.name: Generation of 1898
SPAN 4280.description: Reading and discussion of selected works by Unamuno, Barojo, Valleinclan, Azorin, and A. Machado. Study of the significance of this celebrated generation’s contribution to Hispanic literature and thought.

SPAN 4360.name: Hispanic Short Story
SPAN 4360.description: Readings and discussions of first-rate Hispanic short stories with which to build reading and verbal skills on an advanced level. Provides a wide variety of language learning experiences.

SPAN 4400.name: Topics in Contemporary Culture of Latin America
SPAN 4400.description: Selected topics in Spanish or Latin American cultural production. Contents will vary according to the instructor and the research interests of the class. Possible themes include post World War II artists, literary works, film, or aesthetic movements, the boom, aspects of culture in Spain after Franco (through cinema, through literature, through art). May be repeated once for credit if the topic is different.

SPAN 4420.name: Hispanic/Latino U.S. Literature
SPAN 4420.description: Study of the works of the leading Chicano/a, Puerto Rican, and Cuban-American writers in the United States. Taught in Spanish.  Approved for LAS Cultural Diversity requirement.

SPAN 4430.name: Hispanic Drama
SPAN 4430.description: Theatrical work of the Spanish-Speaking world.

SPAN 4440.name: Hispanic, Chicano/a, and Mexican-American Literature
SPAN 4440.description: The literary manifestations of individuals of Mexican origin in theater, prose, and poetry. Taught in Spanish.

SPAN 4450.name: U.S. - Cuban Culture
SPAN 4450.description: Since the 19th century, Cubans migration to the U.S. has resulted in cultural contributions to the arts, music, literature, and public discourse; this class explores aspects of these works in the context of their production in conversation with American, Cuban, and broader Latino discussions of identity, aesthetics, and thought. Taught in Spanish.

SPAN 4460.name: Studies in U.S.-Mexico Border Literature
SPAN 4460.description: The literary manifestation of U.S-Mexico border writers, including prose, poetry, essays and performance art. Some of the texts will be in Spanish, some will be in English. Taught in Spanish.

SPAN 4510.name: Topics in Contemporary Hispanic Culture
SPAN 4510.description: Reading and discussion of contemporary Hispanic American masterworks. Contextual exploration, analysis, and discussion of contemporary Hispanic American works of art, artistic movements, historical contexts. Content will vary according to instructor and class interests.

SPAN 4610.name: Latin American Authors
SPAN 4610.description: Reading and discussion of selected material.

SPAN 4620.name: Don Quijote I
SPAN 4620.description: Background and study of the first part of Cervantes’ Don Quijote (1605); the 52 chapters.

SPAN 4630.name: Don Quijote II
SPAN 4630.description: Background and study of the second part of Cervantes’ Don Quijote (1615).

SPAN 4650.name: Spanish or Latin American or Chicano Authors
SPAN 4650.description: Offered as three five-week mini-courses (each course carrying 1 credit). This course sequence will deal with three cultural producers of either Spanish or Latin American or Chicano masterpieces. Students are encouraged to take the entire three-course sequence, which will be offered during the regular semester in successive segments during the same day/time block. Consult Course Search on the UCCS website or the MyUCCS Portal for specific topics.

SPAN 4660.name: Spanish-Language Poetry
SPAN 4660.description: Contextual analysis of aspects of Spanish language poetry production. Consult Course Search on the UCCS website or the MyUCCS Portal for specific topics.

SPAN 4970.name: Senior Seminar: Spanish
SPAN 4970.description: Required capstone course for graduate with a major in Spanish. Monographic study of a period, author, genre or topic. Offered once per year in the spring semester. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Summit.
SPAN 4970.prereqs: Five previous literature courses (SPAN 3190, SPAN 3200, and three others)

SPED 1000.name: Career Development and Self Determination
SPED 1000.description: This is a course where instructors will teach students to 1) define and take action on personal goals and 2) communicate clearly about the supports necessary for their success.
SPED 1000.prereqs: Office of Inclusive Service students only

SPED 1010.name: Inclusive Services Senior Capstone
SPED 1010.description: The Inclusive Services Senior capstone course is designed for students who receive services through the Office of Inclusive Services to demonstrate their cumulative learning of their individual area of study, person-driven planning, goals for life after college, and personal transition plan.

SPED 3000.name: dis/Ability Studies in Education
SPED 3000.description: An introduction to how disability, race, class, sexual orientation, and gender are defined, represented, and acted upon in schools today. Students will examine school as a social/political environment where the meaning of disability can be understood in democratic ways.

SPED 3001.name: Introduction to Special Education
SPED 3001.description: This course provides an overview of Special Education. The course emphasizes the history of special education; legislation; implementation of IDEA, current issues; and a survey of exceptionalities. This course is designed to support the Performance-based Standards for Colorado teachers. Thirty (30) hours of field experience required.

SPED 3002.name: Professional Seminar in Special Education
SPED 3002.description: Familiarizes students with professional issues in special education. The areas include: (a) professional dispositions, (b) student diversity, (c) instructional/assistive technology, and (d) professional writing. Teachers must understand academic and professional standards and their relationship to the work environment.

SPED 3003.name: Classroom and Instructional Management
SPED 3003.description: This course will examine evidence-based approaches for providing classroom and instructional management. The emphasis is on (a) effective instructional procedures, (b) individual and classroom behavior management strategies, and (c) principles of applied behavior analysis. Fifteen (15) hours of field experience is required. Meets with Sped 5003.

SPED 3004.name: Self-Determination and Transition
SPED 3004.description: This course presents self-determination and development, implementation, and evaluation of self-management instructional programs for students. Service delivery models, issues, and intervention approaches are examined in light of efficacy research. Emphasis is upon using self-management and learning strategies to facilitate self-determination. Fifteen (15) hours of field experience is required.

SPED 4010.name: Multisensory Structured Language Education
SPED 4010.description: This course focuses on literacy instruction in the components of phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, and comprehension. We will study research evidence and strategies for teaching reading skills explicitly and systematically to students who require intensive intervention.
SPED 4010.prereqs: Praxis or Place Elementary Content Test

SPED 4011.name: Assessment and Instructional Monitoring
SPED 4011.description: This course examines evaluation concepts and assessments attending to curriculum-based individual-referenced measures, standardized assessments, and large-scale criterion-referenced tests characteristic of most statewide programs. Emphasis will be placed on aligning curriculum, instruction, and assessment. Fifteen (15)  hours of field experience is required.

SPED 4012.name: Differentiated Instruction
SPED 4012.description: Builds upon material covered in Multisensory Language (SPED 4010/5010). Topics include systematic, differentiated instruction in syllable types, morphology, prefixes, suffixes, Latin Roots, and Greek combining forms. Students work with a tutorial student and evaluate teaching skills through small group coaching sessions.

SPED 4013.name: Direct Instruction Practicum
SPED 4013.description: This course is for the teacher-in-training to learn and practice effective instructional teaching behaviors (e.g., pacing, transitions, data collection, correction procedures, organization of classroom materials) in school settings and demonstrate proficiency in the planning, delivering, and evaluating reading instruction. Field experience is required.

SPED 4020.name: Significant Support Needs
SPED 4020.description: This course presents the development, implementation,and evaluation of instructional programs for students with severe cognitive and physical needs at the elementary and secondary levels. Service delivery models, issues, and intervention approaches are examined in light of efficacy research. Thirty (30) hours of field experience is required.

SPED 4021.name: Designing Positive Classroom Environments
SPED 4021.description: This course examines positive behavior support from philosophical, theoretical, individual, and systemic perspectives. Emphasizes characteristics of students with challenging behavior, functional behavioral assessment, school-wide, classroom, and non-classroom PBS models and interventions, and models for family and community positive behavioral support. Twenty (20) hours of field experience is required.

SPED 4022.name: Consultation and Collaboration
SPED 4022.description: This course critically analyzes issues, research, implementation approaches, and recommended practices for employing collaborative models to support learning across diverse school and community settings. Students will access and evaluate community resources, develop and maintain interdisciplinary and interagency partnerships. Twenty (20) hours of field experience is required.

SPED 4025.name: Fieldwork in Inclusive Classrooms
SPED 4025.description: Students will work in general education settings to include students with disabilities. Assignments and experiences will focus on providing access to the general education curriculum and connecting students with disabilities to their peers.

SPED 4030.name: Elementary/Secondary Internship
SPED 4030.description: Students are required to apply and integrate research-based practices in an educational setting. Student teachers will work with a wide range of students with special needs in programs that utilize practices congruent with the UCCS Special Education Program. This internship must be completed at the opposite K-12 age range from SPED 4031/5031.

SPED 4031.name: Elementary/Secondary Student Teaching Seminar
SPED 4031.description: Students are required to apply and integrate research-based practices in an educational setting. Student teachers will work with a wide range of students with special needs in programs that utilize practices congruent with the UCCS Special Education Program.
SPED 4031.prereqs: SPED 3004 or SPED 5004, SPED 4010 or SPED 5010, IELM 4025 or TED 5640

SPED 4430.name: TeachSpecialEd.com:  Foundations in Special Education
SPED 4430.description: This course places the history of special education in context of current principles and practices. Presents contributions of advocacy groups relative to legislative accomplishments and addresses important issues, federal laws, and resources for beginning teachers in determining their legal responsibilities. Meets with CURR 4060.

SPED 4440.name: TeachSpecialEd.com: Development and Characteristics of Learners with Exceptional Learning Needs
SPED 4440.description: Focuses on individuals with high-incidence disabilities, including mild mental retardation, learning disabilities, ADHD, and behavioral disorders. Teachers are also introduced to the attributes of students from low-incidence groups. Meets with CURR 4061.

SPED 4460.name: TeachSpecialEd.com:  Assessment for Instructional Planning and Decision Making
SPED 4460.description: Foundations of assessment are addressed from the perspective of instructional planning and decision making. Legal and ethical principles are covered along with the processes of screening, pre-referral, referral and classifications. Attention is given to assessments in LEP development. Meets with CURR 4062.

SPED 4470.name: TeachSpecialEd.com. Instructional Strategies - Creating Environments that Promote Learning
SPED 4470.description: Development of positive learning environments as a strategy for enhancing teaching and learning. Preventive measures in the context of approaches to building positive behavior support. Intervention strategies for problem behavior, along with techniques for promoting social interactions andbehaviors. Meets with CURR 4063.

SPED 4480.name: Teachspecialed.com. Instructional Strategies: Teaching for Results
SPED 4480.description: Planning for effective instruction is the central focus of this course. Instructional planning, organizing and designing instruction, student outcomes instructional principles, and assessing outcomes of effective instruction. Curriculum-based assessment is covered along with the communication of student outcomes. Meets with CURR 4064.

SPED 4560.name: Teachspecialed.com. Instructional Strategies: Improving Basic Reading Skills.
SPED 4560.description: Emphasizes teaching beginning reading and developing reading fluency. Is applicable to teaching students with exceptional learning needs in varied instructional settings. Meets with CURR 4065.

SPED 4570.name: Teachspecialed.com: Instructional Strategies: Improving Reading Comprehension
SPED 4570.description: Provides an overview of reading comprehension with emphasis on teaching students with exceptional learning needs. Attention is given to building a knowledge base and analyzing text to enable comprehension skills and teaching comprehension strategies. Meets with CURR 4066.

SPED 4580.name: Teachspecialed.com: Language and Communication in Diverse Learners
SPED 4580.description: Places the needs of exceptional learners in the larger context of cultural differences and diversity with a focus on language and communication. Language development and communication styles are covered. Teaching second language learners. Augmentative,alternative and assistive communication development is addressed. Meets with CURR 4067.

SPED 4860.name: Teachspecialed.com: Collaboration and Instructional Planning in the Individual EducP
SPED 4860.description: Emphasizes developing standards-based Ieps in accordance with Idea requirements. Introduces modelsof collaboration and highlights developing collaboration skills to enhance the effectiveness of the beginning teacher in development and implementation of Ieps. Meets with CURR 4068.

SPED 4870.name: Teachspecialed.com: Professional and Ethical Practices
SPED 4870.description: Focuses on the ethical standards and principles of the profession. Ethical issues related to assessment, decision making, instruction, working with agencies, and families/guardians of children with exceptional learning needs are covered. Meets with CURR 4069.

SPED 4910.name: Workshop
SPED 4910.description: Designed to allow specific topics and issues to be explored in-depth.

SPED 4950.name: Summer Institutes
SPED 4950.description: Provides participants with a variety of training opportunities that specifically relate to programs, policies, and procedures for working with at-risk students. Participants will have multiple opportunities to reflect on knowledge learned and develop practical application plans. Meets with SPED 5950.

SOWK 1001.name: Introduction to Social Work
SOWK 1001.description: Designed to help students assess their suitability for careers in social work. Focuses on the emergence of the social work profession including the professional mission, knowledge, skills, and values. Practice settings, client groups, helping services, career patterns, and practice methods are also explored. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Society, Health, and Behavior. Course typically offered: Fall, Spring, Summer

SOWK 3001.name: The Helping Relationship I
SOWK 3001.description: Covers basic skills of helping individuals and families in the context of generalist social work practice. Dual emphasis placed on both the knowledge base and the performance of these skills. Assists students in determining their desire to enter the field of social work and prepares students for further educational experiences at the university and in the social work program.

SOWK 3002.name: Human Behavior and the Social Environment
SOWK 3002.description: Explores the interrelatedness of biological, social, cultural, environmental, and psychological factors in human behavior. Considers person-in-environment over the life span with special attention to diversity, impact of racism, sexism, and other sociocultural factors. Integrates knowledge into a social work practice perspective.

SOWK 3003.name: Social Work Research
SOWK 3003.description: An elementary examination of the various methods used in social work research with emphasis on the scientific method and the role of empirical inquiry to evaluate one’s practice and/or social service delivery. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Writing Intensive.

SOWK 3050.name: The Helping Relationship II
SOWK 3050.description: This course builds upon the foundation established in SOWK 3001 (The Helping Relationship I) and is designed to deepen students’ understanding of generalist social work practice with individuals, families, groups, organizations, and communities. Students will develop intermediate communication and assessment skills and begin to explore intervention strategies. There is a strong emphasis on developing the knowledge and skills for effective practice, with a particular focus on preparing students for senior field practice.

SOWK 3268.name: Contemporary Issues in Social and Public Policy
SOWK 3268.description: Examines a number of social policy issues and the social, economic, and political factors that influence policymaking and implementation. Provides an overview of the American system of social and public policy with emphasis on social welfare policy including health, education, welfare (income security policy), and criminal justice. Provides theoretically based models for analysis and presentation of social policy in legislative, administrative, and agency arenas. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Inclusiveness (Global/Diversity).

SOWK 3400.name: Social, Racial, Economic and Environmental Justice
SOWK 3400.description: Examines intersecting and ongoing injustices that result in oppression and racism, including social work’s role and response. Evaluates distribution of power and privilege to promote social justice, reduce inequities and ensure dignity and respect for all. Prepares students to engage in eliminating structural barriers to ensure that social rights are distributed equitably to protect civil, political, economic, social, and cultural human rights. Among the social work skills addressed are ways to advocate for human rights at the individual and system levels and engage in practices that advance human rights to promote social, racial, economic, and environmental justice.

SOWK 4001.name: Individuals, Families, and Groups
SOWK 4001.description: In-depth study of generalist practice with individuals, families, and groups. Practice roles, value dilemmas, and working with people of diverse backgrounds are examined.
SOWK 4001.prereqs: admission to the Bachelor of Social Work Professional program

SOWK 4002.name: Social Work Practice with Organizations and Communities
SOWK 4002.description: In-depth study of generalist practice with organizations and communities, including treatment theories, techniques, and issues. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Writing Intensive.
SOWK 4002.prereqs: admission to the Bachelor of Social Work Professional program

SOWK 4051.name: Child Welfare I: History, Programs, and Policies
SOWK 4051.description: Provides a historic overview and contemporary application of child welfare policy, problems in policy development, and contemporary American child welfare services in both public and private domains. Includes the study of the child welfare system, examining history and both state and federal policies and programs pertinent to child maltreatment and juvenile justice.

SOWK 4052.name: Child Welfare II: Skills and Practice Methods
SOWK 4052.description: Provides an overview of the roles and responsibilities of social workers practicing within the child welfare system. Focuses on mastery of practice skills at a range of levels (e.g., individual, family, and environment) to develop culturally competent child welfare workers. Emphasis on the special challenges, needed skills, and different strategies and interventions in the provision of culturally responsive child welfare services.

SOWK 4053.name: Social Work in Health and Mental Health Settings
SOWK 4053.description: Prepares students for advanced social work practice in health care. Students gain knowledge, skills, and proficiency in applying theoretical models and evidence-based interventions. Focuses on five critical health practice competency areas: psychosocial assessment, treatment interventions, interdisciplinary teamwork, ethics, and leadership.

SOWK 4054.name: Wellness, Recovery, and Integrated Care
SOWK 4054.description: Provides a foundation of practice for students working within the public health, mental health, and integrated health care systems. Focuses on cutting-edge knowledge in wellness and recovery; interacting systems of mind, brain, and body; and evidence-based integrated care interventions aimed at improving the well-being of low-income and vulnerable populations in a new era of health care reform.

SOWK 4055.name: Social Work Practice with Military Families
SOWK 4055.description: Examines the military culture within which military families function and addresses theory-based and research-informed strategies to intervene with military families at both the micro and macro levels of practice.

SOWK 4056.name: Social Work Practice with Service Members and Veterans
SOWK 4056.description: Addresses the needs of active duty, retired, and deployed service members and veterans at different developmental phases of the military life course, both holistically and within the context of their families and communities.

SOWK 4057.name: Family and Child Legal Requirements
SOWK 4057.description: Examines legal principles and procedures relevant to social work practice with families and children including juvenile delinquency, child protection, child adoption, education, and domestic relations. Also covers legal aspects of social work practice including licensing, confidentiality, and professional liability.

SOWK 4058.name: School Social Work Interventions
SOWK 4058.description: Designed to give students the ability to identify, understand, and apply the varied roles of the school social worker.

SOWK 4059.name: Advanced Practice Skills For Social Work
SOWK 4059.description: This undergraduate elective course offers students an in-depth exploration of various practice methods prevalent in the realm of social work. Through a combination of lectures, case studies, and role-playing, students will gain comprehensive knowledge of Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Task-Centered Practice, Solution-Focused Brief Therapy (SFBT), and Acceptance and Commitment Therapy (ACT). The curriculum is designed to not only introduce these methodologies but also to delve deep into their principles, applications, and critiques, enabling students to understand when and how to integrate these techniques effectively in their practice.

SOWK 4060.name: Self-Care Practice for Professional Sustainability
SOWK 4060.description: Research and anecdotal stories have described types of stress, fatigue and burnout experienced by front-line workers. It is important to build self-care strategies before problems start. This course aims to provide front-line workers with the tools and insights needed to maintain their well-being while upholding their commitment to helping others. Students will discover ways to build and grow their own self-care practices, as well as exploring ways to support the formation of a “community of care” that upholds ethical practice and compassionate leadership through an antiracism, diversity, equity, and inclusion (ADEI) lens.

SOWK 4111.name: Social Work Seminar and Practicum I
SOWK 4111.description: First course of the two-course practice sequence. Supervised agency practicum with practice situations for developing professional skills, values, and attitudes for social work practice. Includes concurrent seminar to promote integration of theory and practice and critical examination of oneself as a helping professional. Course requires completion of a minimum of 200 practice hours at an approved social service agency. BSW capstone project preparation will begin in this course.
SOWK 4111.prereqs: admission to the Bachelor of Social Work Professional program; Senior standing; Consent of Instructor required

SOWK 4112.name: Social Work Seminar and Practicum II
SOWK 4112.description: Second course of the two-course practice sequence. Supervised agency practicum with practice situations for developing professional skills, values, and attitudes for social work practice. Includes concurrent seminar to promote integration of theory and practice and critical examination of oneself as a helping professional. Course requires completion of a minimum of 200 practice hours at an approved social service agency. BSW capstone project completion will occur in this course. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Summit.
SOWK 4112.prereqs: Admission to the Bachelor of Social Work Professional program; Senior standing; SOWK 4111; Consent of Instructor required

SOWK 4600.name: Special Topics in Social Work
SOWK 4600.description: Covers emerging developments or specialized content in the field of social work and provides the opportunity to explore significant themes, issues, and problems from a broad interdisciplinary perspective. Topics vary from semester to semester.

SOWK 4840.name: Independent Study in Social Work
SOWK 4840.description: Faculty-guided research in an area of mutual interest to the student and instructor. Students are responsible for selecting their area of inquiry prior to contacting the instructor.
SOWK 4840.prereqs: Junior standing and Consent of instructor required

SOWK 4900.name: Social Work Senior Summit
SOWK 4900.description: In this course, students compile portfolios comprised of artifacts from coursework and field, demonstrating competence in the knowledge, values, and skills necessary for generalist social work practice. Students also prepare for the BSW job market and/or MSW program applications.
SOWK 4900.prereqs: Senior standing and completion of or concurrent enrollment in SOWK 4111 or SOWK 4112

SPTM 1000.name: Introduction to Sport Management
SPTM 1000.description: A survey of the history of modern sport; examination of the foundation, operations, philosophy, and trends of contemporary sport management. Presentation of skills and techniques to prepare students to administer programs in diverse sport settings; issues and complex problems that confront sport leaders are emphasized. Course typically offered: Fall, Spring

SPTM 2000.name: Principles of Sport Law
SPTM 2000.description: Investigation and analysis of the law and legal issues in sport settings. Topics include negligence theory, risk management, common defenses, product liability, insurance, contracts, and implications for event development and operations.
SPTM 2000.prereqs: SPTM 1000, Sophomore Standing, Sport Management Students only

SPTM 2350.name: Sport Science for Sport Administrators
SPTM 2350.description: Integration of exercise training and testing into business practices of sports organizations. Interdisciplinary lecture/lab format introduces and emphasizes roles and impact of human anatomy, exercise physiology, bio-mechanics, growth and development, nutrition, training principles, and drug testing in the development and management of sport. Approved for Compass Curriculum requirement: Explore-Physical and Natural World.

SPTM 2960.name: Pre-internship and Professional Development
SPTM 2960.description: After gaining practical knowledge and hands-on experience through required field experience hours, students will prepare for their internships through several professional development assignments. Students will develop/enhance their cover letter and resume writing skills, complete mock interviews and plan out their remaining course schedule with timing of internship placements in mind.
SPTM 2960.prereqs: SPTM 1000, Sport Management majors only, 50 hours of field experience, 3

SPTM 3960.name: Internship in Sport Management
SPTM 3960.description: Junior-level undergraduate internship opportunity in sport management. Minimum of 150 hours.

SPTM 3961.name: Internship in Sport Management
SPTM 3961.description: Junior-level undergraduate internship opportunity in sport management. Minimum of 150 hours. This course offers full-time student classification due to highly involved and/or non-local internships (Financial Aid Progress Units: 12).

SPTM 3965.name: Practicum in Soccer Management
SPTM 3965.description: Undergraduate practicum for Sport Management students pursuing the Soccer Management Track. Minimum of 150 hours.
SPTM 3965.prereqs: SPTM 2960, Junior standing, Soccer Management majors only

SPTM 3966.name: Practicum in Soccer Management
SPTM 3966.description: Undergraduate practicum for Sport Management students pursuing the Soccer Management Track. Minimum of 150 hours. This course offers full-time student classification due to highly involved and/or non-local internships (Financial Aid Progress Units: 12).
SPTM 3966.prereqs: SPTM 2960, Junior standing, Soccer Management majors only

SPTM 3970.name: Project Based Learning in Sport Management
SPTM 3970.description: Project-based course to blend practical experiential learning through the completion of a project. Projects will be provided for students to select from. Students will meet with their project manager and the designated Sport Management faculty member for a detailed description of the project along with expectations and suggested resources. Students will submit a project that effectively offers solutions or ideas to the given scenario that managers may find beneficial to their organization(s).
SPTM 3970.prereqs: SPTM 2960, Sport Management Students Only, Instructor Consent Required

SPTM 4150.name: Sport Sales and Analytics
SPTM 4150.description: Provides students the skills necessary to use data to cultivate relationships and activation strategies associated with the sport product. Considerable time will be spent on the sales process, data analytics, fundraising, and relationship management as it applies to selling various sport products.
SPTM 4150.coreqs: QUAN 2020, Sport Management students only, Junior standing

SPTM 4200.name: Researching Critical Issues in Sport Management
SPTM 4200.description: The goal of this class is for students to better understand the research process and to apply this to a specific critical issue in the sport management field. The class provides students with tools and insights to help guide personal inquiry and the research process. Students will work in pairs to design, plan, implement and present a bespoke research project focusing on a critical issue in sport management.
SPTM 4200.prereqs: SPTM 4300, Senior standing; SPTM students only

SPTM 4250.name: International and Olympic Sport Development
SPTM 4250.description: This course examines the evolution of modern sport including the development and growth of the Olympic system. It explores the values associated with the system, the range of ethical challenges that confront the system, the conditions that give rise to such problems, and the prospects for the reform of future governance arrangements for international and Olympic sport. Preq., Sport Management students only, Junior standing. Course typically offered: Fall

SPTM 4300.name: Sport Facility and Event Management
SPTM 4300.description: The course provides an overview of planning, development, and operation of sport facilities and sport events. The course includes methods of measuring facility and event performance. Coreq. MKTG 4510, Sport Management students only. Course typically offered: Fall, Spring

SPTM 4350.name: Sport Economics and Finance
SPTM 4350.description: Provides students with the structure necessary to understand the role of a financial manager and the economics of sport in the sports industry.
